I actually asked many friends who turned me on to a dozen screen capture software programs, but many expected a monthly subscription fee. Not buying. So, when a friend suggested Movavi, I was kind of shocked, because I am a Movavi user (Movavi 8) for converting video and audio files but had no idea that they also did video editing and screen capture. The program worked great for my use, and I found myself exploring the video editing capabilities as well. It is very similar to Windows Movie Maker which I've used for years. While I am still playing with the editing suite, and haven't actually saved a movie yet, I can only comment on the ease of the basic use. Nice options for animations, editing, etc. all the basics, so far. But I am not sure how quickly it saves the movie. Still, I have a good feeling I'll be dropping movie Maker and moving to Movavi. I do like that Movavi has two lines for audio. I only wish they offered multiple video lines in case you shot something from multiple views/cameras, so you could line up the video and pick/choose which shot to add you your movie. Still, for the price of the suite, which also offers the ability to convert types if files, you cannot go wrong with this suite!

So, if you're the one who has been the primary user of TurboTax, using it is easier to use than if you are the one who is the secondary user. To be more clear, TT doesn't give you the option to switch who is the primary user (if it refers to you as the spouse or the preparer).

For example, I am getting a divorce. Since my husband wanted his name to be the primary name in the software, his name is first and mine second even though I prepared some of our tax returns. So, in the case of a divorce, when you go to import your information from your joint return from last year, you get 2 options: to manually delete your \\"spouse's\\" information or to start a new return. If you choose the spouse option, TT automatically removed my information and assumed that my husband was the preparer of the return because I was the \\"spouse\\". I typed my name into the personal profile information and replaced his when the opportunity arose, but the software continued to refer to him as the preparer and me as the spouse so when it came time for me to enter my information it assumed I was him. The upshot of this is there is no way for me to import information (profile, investments, employer info, whatever) from last year because TT makes assumptions about who you are and doesn't allow you to change those assumptions. I have to start all over again and type everything in from scratch!

TurboTax PLEASE develop a way to switch who is primary in the software and who is secondary!

I didn't buy this through Amazon, but through the official website and got both the HotSpot+Dispatch combo (lifetime). From my experience, the customer service is a little lacking, which can be quite frustrating if you are confused on how the product works, but the forum has many users that have experiences to help. The software itself? Well I can testify that it works. The HotSpot (Wifi extender) works like a charm. My laptop is able to pick up wifi from a further distance than my phone and tablets so I was able to latch onto the wifi signal and broadcast the signal through my laptop and wow was it awesome. There seemed to be minimal speed reduction, but it worked amazingly. My FAVORITE has got to be the Dispatch. It allows you to connect to multiple connections (wifi, ethernet, etc.) and fuse it all together for one super fast speed. Wifi alone, I got about 1.5-2.0mbps (quite slow) and my phone is on 3g (1.0-2.0mbps). When I used dispatch, it combined those two together and I got a constant 2.5 - 4.0mbps (which is fast in my case because of slow internet before).

Overall, I do recommend the product, do try the free version first to see how it goes. The only reason I bought the pro one was because the free version for dispatch disconnects you after a certain amount of time (I mean it is free). The forum with other users were quite helpful and honestly, it is worth the money. For people that may want to buy the product, there is still a 40% off deal going on.

***5/8/2014***UPDATE Please substitute 4 1/2 stars for 5 mentioned in this review.
Other updates have been posted at the end of this review as I work my way through the product. This one goes up front.

At least up to 2010 (my latest upgrade experience), S&T was backward compatible with routes (.est files) created with older versions. However, once the older file was configured to operate in the newer version, the new file wasn't usable in older versions of the software. For the 2013 version, the older .est files inexplicably are no longer usable and can't be imported from 2010. A similar complaint is mentioned in several other reviews. ***UPDATE 5/17/2014*** After reviewing answers following mine to a question on importing from earlier versions, I began to wonder if you couldn't EXPORT as a GPX from your Older version (if it supports it) and then IMPORT as a GPX to 2013? I already know that as an .est file, 2013 won't import a 2010 file. Had already removed the 2010 trial version and was able to reinstall with 21 of 60 days left.

I learned you CAN import (via GPX) ONLY THE ROUTE from an earlier version (or even another brand of product) that supports EXPORTING to a GPX file. All that is transferred are the origination point, stops that are shown and the destination that are part of the original .est Route Planner screen. The names you gave those points in Route Planner transfer, too. However, ALL OTHER PUSHPINS and associated information that you may have entered or highlighted for scenic points, landmarks, etc., on the map along the way that are not included in the original Route DO NOT transfer.

So, I guess one could conclude that an import to 2013 from an earlier version is a QUALIFIED success. I have many routes annotated on the map with GPS coordinates for interesting locations and attractions, springs found while hiking, etc. While only the ROUTE transferred, the rest of the information did not. The downgrade from 5 to 4 1/2 stars on 5/8 remains unchanged.

Am a user of S&T since 2003 and its stablemate Autoroute (a 60 day trial for navigating Europe). Upgraded to S&T 2006 with the GPS when it became available. In general S&T has guided me all over the US with very little to complain about and have become fairly intimately familiar with both. Realizing 2006 is finally dated, decided to go with S&T 2013. The question was CD version or download?

To start with, I recommend that for any downloaded software purchase on Amazon, go to the mfr's web site and look for a trial version. MS changed their very generous 60 day trial period for past versions (don't know exactly when) and is now 14 days.

With the trial version in hand, set out to see if I would experience the same issues experienced by other reviewers of this product. A few that bothered me were not being able to set pushpins, not being able to drag a route, and not following a major interstate (I91). After 3 days of using the trial, there have been no such issues. For the I91 issue, plotted a course from I95 WB exit 48 all the way to the Canadian border at Derby with the default settings for Preferred Segments. The route transitioned to I91 and stayed on it for its entire 291 mile length. I dragged, reset, dragged again, set pushpins. Not a single hitch. At this point, I already have a 3-fer in favor of the the program.

Am running this program on an Acer C60 with 4 GB RAM and an after market SSD with Windows 7. S&T recognized the GPS puck from 2003, installed the driver and acquired my position surprisingly quickly. Voice navigation was clear and crisp through the AUX input available on one of my vehicles. Way better than a smart phone or other GPS device.

Other reported concerns were downloading from Amazon and activation issues. Since I downloaded the trial from Microsoft first, all I needed was a product key. The product key was shown in the Amazon download page. I copied and pasted the key to an encrypted folder for safe keeping, opened S&T trial and started the activation process, then pasted the key to the first box of the MS activation field. It filled in the rest of the key in the appropriate boxes and in less than two minutes the trial version was activated. The entire process from payment to full activation of the Trial Version was 10 minutes tops over a meager internet connection. (but download of the Trial Version from MS took over 3 hours). So, if there are download issues with Amazon, try the MS webite and get the Trial. Use your product key from the Amazon download page and you should be good to go.

I will be downloading from Amazon to a different computer to test the AMZ download process and the ability to install on multiple computers with the same product key. I can probably do the multiple install with the Trial Version (1.4GB), but want to see if there are any hiccups with Amazon's download process. I also want to see if there is a difference between the MS 1.4 GB download size vs Amazon's 2 GB download. My guess is AMZ's download is exactly the same as Microsoft's Trial Version.

Even if I were limited to a single computer install, my experience with past versions as well as the present one so far are consistent with a 5 star experience. Will be looking at all the remaining reviews this product has garnered to date, to see if reported shortcomings hold true. I would say though, that interface issues (like color/layout) aren't a bother to me unless something just doesn't work. Stay tuned....

*******Update 4/29********
Download, installation and activation- There were no hitches with the Amazon download. Downloaded 32 bit and 64 bit versions. However, if you stop the download, you might have to start the entire process over, including the initial Amazon installer. The download from MS can be paused and resumed in the browser. The AMZ download defaults to 32 bit.

Installed 64 bit on two different W7 computers and a Windows 8.1 Update (1) Pro. The 8.1 installation also recognized the old GPS puck from 2003, installed the driver and also quickly displayed my position. GPS acquisition seems to be much faster than in previous versions for all the computers I tested. As I read the licensing agreement, to be in compliance and avoid legal issues, it can remain only on 2 (1 primary where the software will normally be used and 1 secondary, such as a mobile). There were no activation issues, either. For all activations, pasting the product key avoids input errors for the 25(!) character product key. There is a provision for transferring the software to a third party in the licensing agreement.

The download file size is 1.44GB. The file size shown by Amazon (2GB) is the extracted file size when starting the installation. If you're having trouble with the download, it's less likely to be an Amazon issue. The download stays is your Amazon \\"software library\\" for future use. I put both downloads on a thumb drive as a backup.

User Interface note- The icon for the view (e.g. Navigation/Planning) you're in is highlighted when selected. A nice feature for tired eyes. In 2006 version, it wasn't and I usually hesitated momentarily when switching views. My wife (not as familiar with the software) would hesitate longer. My 5 star experience continues and will revise the review as needed.

I feel sorry for those early adopters that jumped right away only to see the price drop 33% in a really short amount of time. I suppose they could return the software and re-purchase it for the savings but what a hassle. Ah the challenge of price-timing when shopping at Amazon!

As far as reviews go for years I've benefited from reading the reviews on Amazon and truly have been influenced on my purchases by all those comments and thought it was time to pay back for all those reviews I've read without contributing so I'm trying to step-it-up and write more of my own. I buy ALL my products for my own use. I have ZERO bias and give my honest feedback on my actual experiences.

In the case of Quicken Deluxe 2015 I jumped when the price hit $50 which, for me, is a reasonable price for the Deluxe edition.

The installation went fine, the translation of my Quicken 2013 Deluxe file went fine, the Credit Score worked fine, the mobile app (which I never used before) also went fine (and I really like that app), and, finally, the cloud sync also worked fine. I'm not sure why there have been so many challenges by other users but I do realize that computer systems are complex and there are a LOT of variable between various computer systems so maybe I was lucky.

I am a \\"simple\\" user in that I use Quicken to have my own electronic record of our income and expenses AND to sync to our banks to ensure we agree. Any fraud will show up FAST if you sync often and keep an eye on things. For me, Quicken Deluxe does the trick (although I was a real fan of Microsoft Money and was sad when Microsoft dropped support for that product).

I'm not a fan of \\"sun-setting\\" whereby a company discontinues support for software to force an upgrade; however, for me paying $50 every two years to stay current is not really a bad value for software I find so useful. On the flip side I truly do understand if the program is working to YOUR satisfaction it is a disappointment to be forced to upgrade just to be able to continue to sync to your financial institutions. Quicken would tell you \\"No problem, you can always reconcile manually\\" but, yea, right...why would you do that when you can sync and save a TON of time?!? That's one of the main features of this software, after all!

I personally find this a worthy upgrade for $50. More than that...not so much. I've fortunately experienced NONE of the issues that have been reported here. You DO need some level of tech savvy to work with this, or any other complex program, but overall the experience for me has been much more positive than what most of the people here are reporting. I'm running Windows 7, 64 bit, Professional on a custom box.

Best wishes!

Unfortunately, many reviews on software products must be viewed with an eye toward the technology being used and toward the end user. I am NOT saying any review with one star is bogus as it may be quite legitimate. In my opinion, as long as the software is being installed on a machine with the software recommendations as opposed to a machine, for example, that has a small amount of memory and is using a dial-up connection; it should be successful.

Keep in mind the technology as well. In the IT world you get what you pay for which is why you won't find the banks of the world running their credit card applications on a Windows platform (another hint: that is why they use mainframe computers, but I digress)

With regards to the install issues many are having, here is my experience.

Product installed: Quicken Premier 2015
Machine: Lenovo with Windows 7 at the latest OS patch level. Memory is 4 GB running with an Intel Core i7-2600 at 3.4 GHz.
Install methodology employed: Shut down all applications, open installer, open task manager (to monitor memory, I/O, and network traffic)

Observations on the installation:

There were 3 process stated on an informational dialogue box: Backup, Install product, Install patches

The Backup was uneventful.
The install product went well until the progress bar showed 90% completed. It "looked" like it froze but upon looking at the network traffic, there was a steady heartbeat type communication which went on for roughly 5 minutes. I then opened the Windows Resource Monitor to check if the installation processes were still active and it showed activity on the processes (PIDs) being used. Within 1 minute, the installation completed and Quicken finished up.

My guess is that the installation patches were downloaded direct from Intuit and combined with the installation process because I never saw the "Install Patches" highlighted inthe dialogue box.

Software Usage:
It has the same look-and-feel of Quicken 2014. I've been using Quicken since the DOS days but we might be getting to the end-of-life for those "wow" moments. Since I use it for tax preparation, it saves me literally days getting ready for tax time so it is well worth what is paid (and I write off the cost because it is used most exclusively for tax preparation).

Final thoughts:
Be careful of putting too much faith in "the cloud". As a professional IT person, clouds can be hacked. Keeping my personal data local may not be perfect but it doesn't make me the easy target either.

I've been using Quicken 2004 for years (likely since 2004) and love it. But recently my computer crashed and it seemed like the right time for an upgrade so I purchased Quicken Essentials. What a disappointment. Though the interface is sleeker and the program seems to run, or almost glide, more smoothly, the basic functionality that I depended on Quicken for isn't there. One of the functions I appreciated in Quicken 2004 so much was the ability to categorize transactions in splits. Ie, you could enter one payment to a credit card, for say, $500, and then record all of the different categories the payment went to, as well as the amounts, $100 for groceries, $50 for gas, and so on. The new version of Quicken isn't able to do this. If you pull up a category like gas, Quicken includes the TOTAL amount of every split payment that includes $ towards gas. Instead, you're required to create an additional account for your credit card, and track the charges there. That does have some pluses - you can automatically download transactions which can be very convenient, but when it comes to tracking your spending, a charge to your credit card is not the same thing as paying the credit card bill. So, if it's spending/expenses you're trying to track the numbers just don't ad up. Unless that is you you want to enter a separate entry for every single item on the bill as you pay it, which I guess you could also do. That however would make reconciling your accounts tricky, as payments wouldn't easily match up.

There may be a solution to this problem, but that in itself IS another problem with Quicken Essentials. While it looks pretty and has superficial functions like tag clouds (Quicken shows you a cloud with the tags for categories you spend the most on, like on a blog, the words for the categories you spend more on, like gas or groceries, appear larger) it's really hard to get basic information. You can create reports but they don't include the memos you enter along withthe transactions - $50 for gas, Mom's bday. Again, this can make tracking things really difficult. Also, customer support is fairly lacking and instead there's a user community. I know that's standard fare, but it took me a couple of days to sort out the answer above and while users are fairly helpful it does make you feel, as a customer, tossed aside. Why Quicken didn't put the resources it put into building and moderating an online community, into retaining basic functions required for bookkeeping instead is a bit of a puzzle. A few days after buying this version of Quicken I've sadly returned it and requested a refund. I've re-installed my old trusty version, Quicken 2004, instead.

For those that don't know Office 365 is basically a 1 year lease of \\"Office Professional\\", with some bonuses (80 Skype minutes, an additional 20G of sky drive space, and Office on Demand). They want people to go to a leased model - and who can blame them. It provides a steady stream of revenue, and they only have to maintain the \\"latest\\" version. If everyone is on the latest product, no one has to maintain security updates and patches for software that was released years ago.

Also by dangling the \\"5 license carrot\\" this product becomes very appealing - especially to those of us that want the additional software such as outlook / publisher / one note. This breaks down to less than $2 per month per computer - Giving \\"Free\\" a run for it's money.

If you are looking for the 'core' office items (Word / Excel / PowerPoint) to use on one or perhaps two PC's - Simply buy Office Home and Student.

PRO's of 365:

1. Price - If you are comparing 365 to the Office Professional then spending $100 VS $400 (or even $219 for Office Home/Business) is tempting. What really adds to the temptation of 365 is that you can install it on 5 machines as opposed to one machine on the other platforms. So if you need office on your home computer, laptop, and the kids school computer - office 365 may be the route to take; And you would still have 2 licenses left. If you make full use of the 5 licenses you are only paying $1.66 per month per computer.

2. FULL office suite. Your get all 7 software pieces found in Office Pro - Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote, Publisher, Access.

3. Virtual Office - If for whatever reason you don't have your computer with you, you can access 'office on demand'. This will stream a copy of office to any internet connected machine and you can access your files via sky drive. Nice if you are at someones house / public internet terminal.

4. No longer cloud only - In the past 365 was a cloud only app - the software had limited features and capabilities compared to the full desktop versions, and if you didn't have an Internet connection you didn't have Office. No more though, you run the real software on your machine locally - so if you are on a plane, or without internet you can still use the product.

5. \\"Free\\" Upgrades - With 365 you are leasing the latest version. So as long as you maintain your subscription, in a few years when the next version comes out you will be able to upgrade without having to 're-buy' office.

Cons:

1. You are 'locked in' - Every year you must renew your lease if you want continued functionality. You will still be able to view your documents and notes, but if you don't renew you loose the ability to edit them.

2. Tablet support - 365 works well on Win 8 tablets, but no support yet for Android or Apple.

Now, for Tax Year 2014, Intuit has made some significant changes to TT Basic - - and those changes are pretty dramatic for anyone other than a 1040EZ or 1040A Standard Deduction tax filer. I have been pursing genealogical research for over twenty years. I have collected volumes of information about family members and hoped I would one day get around to documenting it all. About ten years ago I realized that I was using an ineffective approach, as most people do. I sought after research software that would help me catalog my sources, and the information they provided, before I would enter my conclusions into a genealogical database. Alas, no such product has existed--until now. Evidentia is that product, and I believe it is going to revolutionize the way genealogists, both professional and amateur, conduct and APPLY their research efforts. It already has, for me.

It is hard to describe what Evidentia actually DOES, but think of it in this way: Let's say that you find three jigsaw puzzles in boxes, but the cover pictures have faded completely and you cannot use them to assemble the puzzles. You dump all three puzzles into one box so you can throw them away, but then realize that there may be valuable information in one of those puzzles. If you dump all of the pieces into Evidentia, one at a time, Evidential will assemble all three of them into finished pictures of what the puzzle was about in the first place.

While the above is a metaphor, it is good description of how Evidentia helps you un-puzzle the ponderables in your research. The more you use it, the more you come to understand its value.

This is my first review on Amazon and I am not affiliated with Evidentia in any way other than being an enthusiastic and satisfied user.

I have a MIDI piano keyboard that only sends MIDI signals (a controller, i.e. no sound module built in). When you start the program for the first time you need to do instrument setup and one step is to choose your MIDI sound source, needed if your keyboard doesn't make sound. I was given two choices, the MIDI interface (Scarlet 2i4) that I use for music software called Cubase (and what my keyboard is connected to), and the Microsoft GS Wavetable Synth. The latter comes with Windows. I selected that and discovered the sound was delayed enough on every notes to make it unusable. That's called latency, and I have read elsewhere that this MS sound 'module' has about 150 ms of latency.

Fortunately for me I was able to select the other MIDI interface and go through Cubase and a virtual instrument there with no latency, but you may not have that option.

The best keyboard for this program is probably a MIDI keyboard that has it's own sound source AND a MIDI output, OR a MIDI controller keyboard like mine PLUS a physical synthesizer module like a Roland JV-1080 (no latency hooked directly). Then you would need two MIDI outs on the keyboard, one for the synth module and one for your computer and thus the program.

Hope this helps someone in this specific situation.

The projected balance chart is a very big feature that I look at all the time to let me know how I am doing, and shows me if I need to make some small adjustments to future bill payment dates or amounts to avoid going into the red at a later time. Microsoft Money had a feature where you could enter budget amounts for things like gas, groceries, spending, etc. on a weekly basis, and it would automatically add those items to your scheduled bills/deposits area. Of course, this meant that those amounts would also automatically adjust your projected balance chart to give you an accurate picture of your balance in the future. Additionally, as you spent money in those particular budget categories during the week, it would automatically deduct those amounts from your weekly amounts that you had setup so you always knew how much money you had left for a given week in those categories.  To make it work in Quicken, what you have to do is manually create \\"bills\\" for each of those budgeted weekly amounts, and then manually deduct from them as you spend in those categories during the week. It can be done, and I am used to it now, but Money made it so much more convenient.  Anyway, overall I like Quicken. I wouldn't know what to do if I didn't have software like this to help manage my money. But I am very disappointed with what this new version offers over Quicken 11.

I own Powerdvd 11 ultra but I just want to warn potential purchasers what they could be letting themselves in for. Whether you intend to pick this up from Amazon or from Cyberlink themselves, be aware that from version 12 onwards Cyberlink has included the horror which is called Cinavia. This is basically protection against pirated movies and sits within the audio track. Many movies at the cinema now contain this and anyone smuggling a camcorder into there local cinema will find it can effect them too. After approx 20 mins the audio will mute and a message will appear telling them what has happened. When used with PowerDVD 12 or 13, this does effect original purchased movies as well, but only if they are using programs such as Anydvd-HD which is used to make your pc region free as well as cope with the latest movie protection etc. It is Anydvd-HD which is falsely alerting the protection, not the movie. If you have no intention of using Anydvd-HD then it doesn't really effect you, though it's worth saying that there is a feature within it to circumvent Cinavia, but is just a work around and does not remove the protection all together. Some original blu-ray 3D movies I own clearly label 'Cinavia' at the bottom of the case on the rear side. Not all do but movies like 'Hotel Translyvania' is one such title. Also note that the PS3 has Cinavia in-built as well. For me I am staying with Powerdvd 11 for this exact reason. Oh, and some other players such as TMT6 also contain this protection. Better to check first before parting with your hard earned ca$h. Plenty of information online about Cinavia (you can check Powerdvd and Anydvd forums etc). Hope this helps you!

My wife is a native Telugu speaker. I purchased Instant Immersion Telugu Level 1 to help me (a native English speaker) learn her mother tongue. After I downloaded the program, my wife and I went through a few of the vocabulary lists together. It only took a few minutes for me to realize I'd thrown $30 out the window - every few words or phrases my wife would either get a confused look on her face or burst out laughing. Many of the translations, it turns out, are wrong, and some are simply absurd. Examples -

- \\"Left\\" and \\"right\\" are presented together in the course, obviously connoting the relative directions, as in \\"left turn\\" and \\"right turn.\\" However, the Telugu word presented as the translation of \\"left\\" means \\"to leave\\" or \\"let go\\" and has nothing to do with the direction \\"left.\\" Similarly, the word presented as the Telugu equivalent of \\"right\\" only means \\"right\\" in the sense of \\"correct\\"; the Telugu word for the direction \\"right\\" is something completely different than what's presented here.

- Instant Immersion's Telugu translation for \\"Cheers!\\" is an artificial construction for a term that doesn't exist in Telugu. Literally, the Telugu that's presented translates back into English as something to the effect of \\"Let us touch cups together,\\" which my wife assures me sounds even more absurd in Telugu than it does in English.

- Instant Immersion's Telugu translation for \\"Thank you\\" means \\"salutations\\" and not \\"thanks.\\" According to my wife, no one speaking any dialect of Telugu would use Instant Immersion's term to express thanks.

The above are just a sample of the problems we came across in this software. Though we didn't go through the entire course, it seems likely, if not probable, that it's riddled with hundreds of issues like these.

Instant Immersion's Telugu Level 1 seems to have been produced with little concern for accuracy and appears to rely on the translations of native Telugu speakers who did not understand English well enough to know what words they were being asked to say.

Synopsis: I upgraded from Quicken 11 on 02 JAN 2013 and I have had none of the issues cited in the other reviews. Install was flawless and no issues running. Product still only gets four stars because they refuse to incorporate stock/index option trades, which I do a lot of, in the transactions portion of the software which is ridiculous for something touting itself as \\"investment\\" software. Still worth it though for everything else, especially if it is on sale.

Long Version:

I have read the other reviews on here and so I was very tentative about purchasing this version but they had a recent offer for 50% off so I figured it was worth the risk. I will try to classify what I thought were the typical issues cited in other reviews and try to keep it brief.

Install/Upgrade Issues: I have data dating back to 1996 and all of it was incorporated with no errors and/or glitches. Not sure if it may be dependent on the quality of Qdata file of the previous verson (I back mine up frequently), type of system (Windows XP, Vista, etc.), or maybe power of the computer (graphics, etc. but doubt this would be the issue). I have Vista 64-bit (yes, one of the few lucky enough to time buying a computer with Vista on it) but again, no issues.

Slow processing of transactions: I have many accounts, transactions, etc. dating back to 1996 and does every transaction get processed at the speed of light? No. I have had choppiness in all versions of Quicken that I have used but overall this speed in this version is no worse then Q2011 version and for the most part I have had relatively quick response times. I am guessing that this is probably mostly correlated to the computing power and system memory free space being consumed by other programs and Quicken. I have a gaming level computer (e.g., lots of processing power and a NVIDIA graphics card) so that may be why I have not had the issues of others but I don't think a basic software program should be that dependent on hardware.

Mobile/Cloud Sync: This was the main reason I took a shot at the upgrade and it has not disappointed! I have been able to enter transactions on the road into my IPhone 5 and come home and sync all of my accounts with no issues or glitches (yet anyway). You do have to manually click a few buttons for the Sync to occur and it is not at blazing speed (but I have DSL so that can contribute to slowness) but it is so worth it versus having to go through receipts or notes and manually enter transactions.

Budgets/Reports Issues: I had no issues with my budgets or customized reports showing up after upgrading but I only use a couple of the customized reports.

Passwords: I had no issues with passwords (e.g., vault, etc.) not working or having to change them from previous version Q2011P.

Tech Support: I can't comment on it as I haven't needed it but don't want to jinx it either!

Lack of Value in Upgrade: I agree with some of the sentiment from the vetern users and \\"loyal\\" upgraders that there is not a dramatic difference between the previous few versions other than the mobil sync/cloud for the full price of the upgrade and they really shouldn't have had that many bug/issues. Thus, I would suggest waiting it out for another 50% or more off sale or perhaps the next version if you are not a frequent mobil/cloud user or don't have a smart tablet/phone.

Overall: Perhaps, they had fixed many of the issues by the time I downloaded it and/or I got lucky with my data conversions but I am really satisfied with the performence overall and especially the mobile feature.

Works much better on a Mac than Windows because you can actually move stuff into directories that sync like Dropbox. But it's a complete fail on Windows. The desktop app is pointless. It allows you to drag and drop files, but you don't get to tell them where to go, nor do you have access to your files and folders on the cloud without proceeding to the web, where you then have to manually select and browse to where you want to move and download your files. There isn't even a way to use desktop syncing software because there is no "amazon cloud" drive to sync to on the Windows desktop. It's ridiculous and this is leaving Amazon almost completely out of the cloud competition. All the free space in the world doesn't make up for the pathetic interface. What's so frustrating is that it seems the infrastructure is there, it's just not giving you full access that causes the hang up. Same with their cloud music player. I love having access to all of my music, but the lack of features in the player and complicated functionality (how in the world do you remove something from the library?!) is just intolerable. I can't imagine that the photo library is going to improve much either. Amazon really needs to get their stuff together, because they are completely missing the boat on this one.   *****UPDATE******  Ok, so the reason I was getting the directories on my Mac was because that was an old install. So this is to confirm that the available app for Mac works the same as Windows.  HOWEVER, after a loooooooot of digging and researching and trial and error, I think I'm starting to realize why the change was made. I gather that the idea is to be able to collect all your data from various sources and allow you to access from anywhere (like every cloud does); BUT, it is actually preventing you from syncing all of your machines or devices with it because you could potentially be putting an incredible excess of data on every system. This is actually a valid reason for not wanting to use a lot of cloud services. It's also not a very good system, and sometimes not even possible, to move your data to a specific local cloud directory to get it to sync. So while I think Amazon caught onto this in time for the big "unlimited data" push, they haven't offered very good alternatives. So far, the only thing I've found to work is Allway Sync, which takes advantage of the Amazon Cloud Drive API that is now available to allow you to setup syncing. I'm trying it out now, and it seems to be working ok, but this only runs on Windows; I'm really needing something to work like this on Mac. I think it will soon be more accessible, but for now it's amazing how little information there is to try and access this cloud drive! The other issue, is well...what happens next. So you sync or backup all your data, and then you move to another machine where you need to access it. Again, that Amazon desktop app is almost useless. The only thing it's really good for is being able to toss stuff up to the drive, like in an emergency, in a completely unorganized fashion. You hope it all gets there because there's no cancelling or pausing, and you'll just have to remember to go online at some point and move it to where it actually belongs. If you want to retrieve any of your data, you basically have to go online, browse, select your files or folders, choose download, which then saves your files as an archive to your downloads folder, which you then have to extract and move to where it belongs. It's painful. Again, you could use Allway Sync (or hopefully something else that works as well) to simply do all this for you, but shame on Amazon for not making this process just a tiny bit more simple for its users. Would it really even be so much to ask to retain the dropbox type folder sync structure, and just have the option to flag how things get synced and unsynced? (yes, I want to always sync from here, no I do not want to ever download this directory to this machine).I wonder if Amazon just assumes that too many people will upload several terabytes of data which would then get unknowingly pushed around between too many devices, and wreak havoc on every server. Because the unlimited plans are so affordable, maybe that's why if you really want to use them, you have to do enough research to actually figure out HOW to properly use them! There just has to be a better way! I think Amazon was in a rush to try and beat out the cloud competition, without flushing out a good consumer-friendly plan. I personally do still have some faith that this could end up being a great solution for me, but it has to get better.

Update 11/10/2016: -------------------------------------  I am updating my review to reflect changes in the Creative Cloud Products.  I use Windows 10 Pro 64 bit, so finding good 3rd party commercial software for web design has been a challenge as most are designed for the Mac.   Creative Cloud is primarily a professional's suite of software. If you are not intending to use the products for work or freelance then I would suggest avoiding Adobe's Creative Cloud unless you have the funds to spare. If you are or have used their software I highly recommend exporting in standards output such as css, html, png, svg  eg... and compatible versions of PDF and PSD files. This way if you lose access or can't load Adobe's software you can still load the work files into another application.  The proprietary file complaint is valid but if you export into common file formats you will not lose any work.  As of the end of 2016 Adobe has revamped their entire suite of offerings. They have eliminated entirely the useful web design software "Edge" projects and cut back and streamlined Dreamweaver and their other design apps.  This puts these in-line with many open source software and offerings from other companies that either do not have a subscription model or a choice between one off purchase with upgrade offers as new version are available OR an subscription model which you choose which you prefer.  Due to the changes in the Adobe line of products I personally have found better options elsewhere for most of the web and graphic design work I do.  There are options now that were not available earlier in 2016 and previous for windows based software so if you do not want to be tied to Adobe's Subscription model you no longer need to choose this company.  I have set my subscription to not renew and will see how that goes when my subscription ends, others have complained of cancellation not going through.  For the vast majority of the current adobe products, now at the end of 2016, there are better and more powerful options available such as from Affinity and Smith Micro as well as open source options including Brackets for coding web pages directly.   Hitfilm and Resolve are alternative video and special effects software with more bang for the buck and easier to use. These are alternatives and don't match up directly with adobe's software so don't look at it as better or worse just different but allowing to do similar things.  For me Creative Cloud is a set of tools and like any tool you will occasionally look around to see if there is something else better for the job at hand. I have discovered better options that are easier and do more and support is easier to deal with especially when they actually know the products which Adobe's support do not. Hard to answer questions or solve issues when they don't even know how the software works.  I like the Creative Cloud but like I said the software has recently changed and been cut back to the point I can do exactly the same thing with strictly open source software now and 3rd Party software that is the cost of less than one months fee or 3 months worth of CC subscription.  Not worth it for me any longer.  I may look back in the future to the Adobe's product line but for now I am moving on as the software really has become just like anything else out there. Nothing special here anymore.  Tip:  Pay attention to the subscription version for the price you have chosen. Lower price tends to be locked to a 12 month contract.  No such thing as one time only for lower price with Adobe at least not in 2016.  ------------------------------------------------ Original Review - ( 2014 ) ------------------------------------------------  I have been a subscriber to Adobe's Creative Cloud since it started.  During that time they have consistently updated the software and come out with 4 or 5 new software only offered through the subscription service.  Not all the updates were that great but bug fixes and some ofof the new features added have been useful.  Comparing Creative Cloud version of some of the titles in CS6 the changes for example in Flash Pro have been a down grade in some respects.  Photoshop has had a few features added that are nice but for the most part the CS6 version works well as is.  The Creative Cloud only apps like Muse are nice if you want to put together an html based site pretty quickly.  Basically everything in the Masters Collection and then some is what you get with the monthly or annual subscription, instead of $2500 you pay $600 per year and they do update the software pretty regularly so for the updates and bug fixes it is worth it.  A lot of people don't like the subscription service and complain that the new features added and bug fixes are not worth the ongoing expense of this service and prefer the one time payment of CS6.  I can't see anything wrong with that.  If you are only going to be using one or two software and not really use much more of the offerings than that, then I would say this would be a waste of money for you.  If you are going to be using Photoshop, Dreamweaver, Acrobat and 3 or 4 more of the applications then it may be worth it for you.  For me I create websites, do youtube video's and create video and audio products the entire creative cloud is very nice.  If you aren't going to be using the software on a regular basis then $600 a year may not be worth it to you.  It is sort of a forced situation where if you sign up you have two choices, pay month to month without a contract for $80 a month or go with a annual contract for $50 a month.  There are first year discounts for various pre-creative cloud product owners and students but those end after the first year and then regular price is $50 a month.  Students may get a special price on going as long as they are enrolled in school but as I am not a student I don't know for sure what those prices are.  You can install applications on as many computers as you want but you can only have two computers activated at one time.  You just signout of creative cloud desktop on a computer and then sign in on another one to begin using the software if you have gone beyond the two activations.  It isn't that big of a deal, unless you need to have them running at the sametime then you won't be allowed to.  You can ask for more activations but no guarantee they will add more for you but it has happened for some.  Once a month the activation software will run and verify you have an active subscription, this requires an internet connection.  Sometimes this happens more than once a month and it can lock you out of the software until it does verify.  Sometimes your login details can be lost from the creative cloud desktop which forces you to retype your adobe id email and password for your Adobe account. This is annoying and has happened to me several times a day for days then it stops asking me and just stays logged in, seems to be an intermittent problem.  Every so often individual apps will ask to be registered, is not suppose to happen but it does.  Isn't a big deal, just click a button and it does it but it can be annoying. Also requires an active internet connection.  Support is horrible, I can't understand phone support and they keep repeating what I say and end up just randomly picking a problem out of their scripts to define the problem I am having. Is not useful and wastes a lot of time.  After the Adobe break in my credit card was canceled which forced me to contact Adobe and they gave me two months credit to give me time to get a new card and to I guess appease me for my trouble.  The problem is you only get a maximum of two months of credit from Adobe and after that they won't issue any more.  I ended up buying a new subscription from Amazon because I was not going to give my new card to Adobe and they canceled my original subscription.  The problem here is that you can't use an account that already has an Adobe Creative Cloud subscriptionso I had to use another account or create a new one.  I ended up doing that and then contacting Adobe and they canceled my subscription through them.  This leaves me with two Adobe accounts but now Amazon is handling the payment charges and not Adobe, I am happy about that but not having two accounts at Adobe.  If you choose to do the samething, switch from Adobe charging your credit card to Amazon charging your credit card then you have to create or use a different Adobe account and pay Amazon first, then have Adobe cancel your first subscription.  They ask for  a 24 character redemption code to verify but Amazon subscription does not use them so you have to verify with the person some other way.  Phone support just does not understand this and won't do anything to help you from my experience, chat support is a little better and that is how I got this resolved.  I do use Adobe's software on a regular basis so for me having access to all their software for $600 a year is worth it, for others it may not be.  If you are a hobbyist or someone that doesn't use the software that much then it probably like I said above is not something you want to get involved with.  If you cancel while under the annual contract then you pay 50% of the remaining balance for the year whether you use it or not.  Just walk into this wide eyed and know exactly what you are getting into and what you will be using the software for.  I am happy with the software and for me it is worth it. I like having the software updated and new features and new software added but sometimes things aren't all that great and the beta software like  Edge Reflow or their new WYSWYG Website software Muse is buggy until they come out with the next version or bug updates, sometimes even then the issues stick around.  Eventually they fix it but it can take awhile, some issues though are just their by design because the designers have their way of doing things and you have yours, the designers win out no matter the number of complaints and feature requests.  The beta programs are interesting to participate in, I do it as little as possible if I can help it.  Overall I like the Creative Cloud and I find it economical versus paying $2500 for masters collection of CS6.  Many don't agree which is fine, it all depends on what and how you use the applications.  I have gone a month or two without even opening one and then all of a sudden I am consistently using 5 or 6 with 3 or 4 being used simultaneously.  Some of the software like Premiere and After Effects I just can't get into so I purchased 3rd Party software for half the price of the stand alone and am consistently using Photoshop, Audition and several other software to help create what I create.  Though it is nice to know After Effects and Premiere are there if I want to learn them, I don't live in Adobe software I just use the tools that work and 70% of the software I use is Adobe so $50 a month is worth it for that.  Turn the autorenewal off if you can and decide at the annual renewal date if it is worth it to continue or not. I just can't find any real alternatives to the software I use regularly or I would probably switch from CC as well.  I do use Open Source and paid 3rd Party Software I just keep returning to Adobe's because it is easier to do things or impossible to do in alternate software.  The haters and complainers talking people away from the subscription some of their points are valid some are just personal biases or vindictiveness over Adobe as a company.  I am not a personal fan of Adobe myself but in my world the software is just a tool, these tools are really good and though some don't work how I prefer them to they do get the job done.  As long as you go into these subscriptions with eyes open and know exactly what to expect then weigh your uses with the price and see if it is worth it to you. You can just pay month to month without having any contract but you pay additional for that privilege, if you only need it for a project or two that maybe the better way to go for you.

The purpose of this software is for personal financial management not for creating all sorts of accounting journals and ledgers. Corporations and other more complex organzations typically have customized software and built on modules to their software to acheive their needs. I think that Intuit would be served best if they remembered who their audience is. Instead of building a system that treats balance sheet transactions differently than income statement transaction, they should look at what is actually occuring (i.e. a credit to a personal cash account IS an expense to individuals!!!) The system will direct you to set up a loan with a corresponding asset and liability. No problem here. However, once you try to budget for a payment, the system can't understand that a transfer from your asset account to reduce the liability is a payment. You would think that if they built the system to handle a mortgage, they would allow you to budget for it. Unfortunately they do not. As a new user, I found Quicken 2013 difficult to get fully up and running. Specifically, it was difficult to add enough past transaction history into Quicken to perform reasonable analyses (two years in my case). The connection to my bank and download of accounts was a snap, but since Wells Fargo only provided the last 90 days of transactions and VISA only the last 60 days, I spent the next week trying to learn how to import the rest. After several failed attempts, exhaustive internet searches for help, and after purchasing several converters from ProperSoft, I finally got everything to work.

Recommendations to new users: don't use the automatic setup feature. Instead: (1) choose the date range you want* and download QFX files from your bank to your computer, (2) import the files into Quicken using Web Connect (not Express Web Connect) - this prevents connection to your bank during import, (3) make sure the imports look good, (4) go to Tools/Account-List, and for each account click Edit, go to the Online Services tab, and change the connection method to Express Web Connect or Direct Connect as desired. At this point you are ready for your first automatic update with your bank. Do the update and check the accounts (you will probably need to change your \\"Opening Balance\\" to get the right current balance).

* Note that to be able to import QFX files using Web Connect, my bank (and Quicken) required that the desired start date and balance correspond to the start date and balance on a past monthly statement.

Adding sufficient Credit Account history is similar but a little harder. Your bank may not even let you download more than 60 days directly, so you will first need to manually cut and paste data from old statements into a spreadsheet, format the data for CSV to QIF conversion, buy a converter (ProperSoft CSV2QIF converter works well), convert the data, and import the QIF file into Quicken.

Recommendations to Quicken (and associated financial institutions): (1) provide at least two years of transaction history for Quicken automatic set up (this includes VISA and the like), (2) if you can't do recommendation 1, then add more comprehensive set up instructions and add capability for Quicken to import csv files (or provide converters with new orders).

Background: After having had a PC's SSD fail (data was backed up), we were only trying to take a system image of a Windows 7 laptop (not having issues), put that on an external drive, and transfer it to a new Windows 8.1 machine. After the 1st migration, the brand new machine indicated trouble at Windows startup, and attempted to repair itself but couldn't. The only thing I could do to start Windows was to either 'refresh' (keep the files but undo the changes in applications) or 'reset' (bring the machine back to factory settings). I did the 'refresh' in order to start Windows, but that beat the purpose of this software by wiping all the apps. (The ones I chose for transfer were all supposedly compatible with the new OS.)

Thinking that may have been because I tried migrating multiple drives/partitions at once (although the company gives precise instructions how to do so, which I followed to the letter), I gave it a second go, this time just choosing the old main C:\ drive with applications (mounted VHD). Same problem - after finishing the process, Windows 8.1 wouldn't start.

At one point I contacted the tech support phone number. From the name of the rep & accent I'd guess it's answered in India. Which I wouldn't mind, if the service is courteous and competent. The rep was convinced the old PC (the one migrating the image from) was the issue, although I tried to tell himwe took the image from the machine that wasn't having issues. He insisted I should install a 'small piece of software' for him to diagnose the problem. This was my husband's laptop, and he had many windows open (he's a game developer), so I didn't want to close the programs to run the diagnostics as he was gone at the time. So I didn't go through the entire process, but that was also partially because I was a bit taken aback when the rep kept asking me, "Are you Asian?" after I gave him my name. At first I didn't answer since that wasn't relevant to my inquiry, but he repeated the question (as if that should make us buddies??). It was strange to be asked such things in a tech support call, and as I wasn't able to tell what he could do with the system info sharing software, I hung up.

Afterward, I reset the new PC to factory setting, because I didn't want to mess up the boot record/wanted a clean start, and just used Windows Easy Transfer (built-in, free) to transfer the files only. Then installed all the applications myself. The failed PCmover process took 2-3 hours of my time and only broke the Windows startup; it may have taken slightly longer to re-do it with Windows Easy Transfer, but it didn't introduce any startup error in the new PC, so that felt much better.

Maybe if you have a simple, one-drive (image)-to-another-drive migration with most common productivity software, this might work. I wouldn't try mounting multiple disk images. I have used this for quite a few years, and bought this years version from the DVD they sent me.

I had two problems, both annoying, and one potentially serious.

1) Since I had the first cut, there were several updates. I could not install the first update at all, and they had to send me a new version of the software with the updates installed. Later, there was another update, and I could not install that either, that is, until I disabled my anti-virus software. Then the update was successful. This is annoying, and potentially very annoying if it happens near April 15. And I bet most people won't think of this.

2) I live in Pennsylvania, and we have some income from small trusts. These come with a K-1 form for the federal return, and an RK-1 for the state return. H&R Block passes the income from the K-1 to the state return and then applies the income info from the RK-1 return. In past years, it has, within the state program, reversed the K-1 amounts, but not this year! If I hadn't caught the discrepancy, we would have paid Pennsylvania tax on this income TWICE.

I was reluctant to spend a huge amount of time online with H&R Block, so resolved this by making a copy of the tax file and then deleting the K-1 info from that copy, thus eliminating the chance that it could be counted twice. To demonstrate that this would work, I did the same thing with a copy of the 2013 tax file, and decided that my workaround worked.

This may only be a problem in Pennsylvania, but you can see that this is a problem that many people may not see and so may pay more to the state than they should. I doubt the state would catch it.

Therefore, three stars for this year.

This is a tale of two cities/products: the first is of a company that chose potential profits over serving a loyal customer base, and the second of an updated product that actually worked flawlessly. Like many other people, I have used Turbotax for a number of years and was largely quite satisfied with it and had no interest is even considering another tax filing software product. However, Intuit's recent decision to remove functionality from the so-called "Deluxe" version of the software (i.e., remove Schedules C, D, & E), and it's initial boneheaded corporate explanation for its money-grab, made me search for other products including H&R Block and TaxAct, etc. Further, I began to follow the outrage of many thousands of previously loyal Turbotax customers on Amazon and other social media sites. It became a daily activity to watch the protest and revolt of customers. The number of 1-star reviews on Amazon grew from hundreds to thousands. This may be one of the most vilified products in the history of modern capitalism. Truly a corporate blunder of epic proportions, and all self-inflicted by Intuit. The company truly deserved the scorn from its previously loyal customers.
With that said, I read all the reviews of all the other major tax software products and seriously considered going with H&R Block. However, I have previously had good experiences with Turbotax and liked its user interface. With the restoration on 2/7/2015 of Schedules C, D, & E to the 'Deluxe" version of Turbotax, I decided to go ahead and try it again, knowing that I could either return it or still use H&R Block if Turbotax failed to deliver.
So, I purchased 'Deluxe' for Mac on 2/7/2015 on Amazon, downloaded it without any problems; it then did an automatic update when it first launched, and then I did my taxes. In the middle of the process, it recognized that I needed Schedule D, and it "upgraded" to "Premier" without any difficulties and at no charge. Itelectronically obtained from my investment broker all stock dividends, interest payments, etc. and entered them correctly into the tax filing. I completed my taxes within an hour, e-filed both the federal and state returns, which were subsequently accepted by the respective federal and state entities. So, the download process working flawlessly, the software also worked without any problems, including the automatic upgrade to Premier and e-filing of the federal and state returns.
How to rate such an experience. I'd give the software itself 5-stars, but Intuit and its money-grabbing, customer disrespecting ways - well, I'd give negative stars if it were possible. They did make amends, but it wasn't because they were serving their customers; rather, they changed only because their loyal customers revolted against their ineptitude and arguablely their corporate greed. If I was on Intuit's Board of Directors, I would vote to change management including the CEO and Turbotax Division Director.

Well, taxes are done, and I’d like to share my first-time experience with H & R Deluxe with One State.  I had previously used Turbotax Deluxe with One State for over 20 yrs (since it was distributed on floppy disks).  Over the years, the price of Turbotax has shot up, and the software has become bloated.  And this year, Turbotax pulled a faux pas extraordinaire that caused many loyal users like myself to desert to alternatives.  I bought the PC download version of H & R Deluxe with One State from Amazon for $29.99.  A good price.  Installation went without a hitch (I’m running Windows 7 Home).  Importing the 2013 Turbotax returns also went without a hitch.  The user interface is similar to the Turbotax user interface before Turbotax introduced the GPS interface.  For me that’s good news, because I consider the GPS interface to be bloated.  I prepared a federal and a NY state return for my daughter.  NY requires electronic filing if you use major tax prep software.  And NY requires that there be no fee for electronic filing.  I electronically filed my daughter’s federal and NY state returns without a hitch.  The software includes 5 federal electronic filings without additional fees; state electronic filings normally cost $19.95 each, but the software properly recognized that there is no charge for a NY state electronic filing.  If I needed to file only a single state return, I would rate this product a 5.  As a side note, H & R has far fewer updates than Turbotax; not sure whether that’s good or bad.  I downgraded the rating to a 3, however, for the way the product handles (or, rather, mishandles) filings with two state returns.  First off, the software to prepare an additional state return costs a whopping $39.95 each; and that does not include electronic filing.  But this was the first year in which I had to file both a NJ (resident) and a NY (non-resident) state return.  And I figured it would be worth the extra cost to have software coordinate the returns.  Unfortunately, the numbers came out bizarre.  I ended up wading through the NJ and NY state websites for detailed instructions.  The NY instructions were confusing.  Fortunately, the NJ instructions had a clear explanation of the NJ forms and of how to deal with NY tax.  I needed to manually override some numbers in the NJ forms.  I decided to electronically file all the returns.  The federal filing went without a hitch.  The NY filing produced an error message that I needed to file by paper because of my particular filing scenario.  When I printed out the paper return, there was also a warning page stating that I was required to file electronically.  I mailed in the paper return with a note stating that I had tried to file electronically but it was rejected.  Keeping my fingers crossed.  I don’t hold H & R responsible for the issues with NY state electronic filing.  The NJ filing also produced an error message that I needed to file by paper because I had manually overridden some entries.  I do hold H & R responsible for the issues with NJ state electronic filing, because if the software had crunched the numbers properly, I wouldn’t have needed to manually override entries.  One minor gripe concerning paper filing of state returns.  Depending on your particular circumstances, you may need to include copies of certain federal forms with the state return.  With Turbotax, when you print the forms required for state filing, any required federal forms are automatically included.  With H & R, when you print the forms required for state filing, you get a checklist indicating that additional federal forms need to be printed.  You then need to manually select and print the required federal forms.  Note:  I don’t know whether Turbotax handles two state returns any better; as I mentioned, this was the first year I had to do that.  But I saw similar complaints in their reviews.

I was looking for a Windows 8 product to replace my Ulead Videostudio 11, which sadly does not support my 64 bit Windows 8.  Unfortunately, Corel bought Ulead and the follow-on products are FUBAR. You can see some examples of those at [...]. I absolutely LOVE the interface on this product....the expandable timeline is the best feature.  Videostudio had a nice time line, but it wasn't expandable.  Nice transition effects, intuitive use of the timeline, captions, anything you could want.  I was impressed!!  The first problem I ran into was that music played on after I set it to end.  Turns out that is a \\"feature\\" that will fill the play time of the slides automatically; including playing over the audio on the video clips! Be sure to go to \\"Settings\\" and turn that off before you start using the product or it will have you scratching your head until you figure it out. With such a nice timeline, I can see no reason for this \\"feature\\", much less have the default \\"on\\", but once you know about it, no big deal. The next \\"feature\\" I encountered was that there is apparently a built-in audio fade on the video clips.  This means that if there is narrative on the very end of a clip, you will lose it in the audio fade. This also creates problems when you are splicing clips together with no transition. I could find no way to turn this off.  That alone made the product unusable for me, but I guess if you are using only images, you don't care. After creating a slideshow, it looked really nice....beautiful preview window, you can drag the time line pointer to play anywhere in the slideshow, delete transitions, text, really nice!  OK, time to try burning a DVD.  I first created a .iso file (DVD image) The product creates some really nice DVD menus, with the option to use images, thumbnails, add your own text, etc.  Again I was impressed! The .iso image played nicely on my PC with VLC.  Next I burned a DVD from the .iso file.  Again it played nicely on my PC with VLC. The final test was to see if it worked on my TOSHIBA BD3000 Blu-Ray DVD player.  Playing it there resulted in some serious issues.  First, the audio was choppy and broken up badly...VERY badly! The DVD had three slideshows on it because I wanted to see how the menus worked.  Here again, serious problems. The DVD menu button, which returns you to the root menu did not work. Just to be sure I wasn't having problems my DVD drivers or burner, I repeated the above tests on a Windows 7 machine with the same results.  Totally unusable DVD burn.    After trading a number of emails with a very nice lady who promptly responded to my support request, she finally said \\"We don't support Blu-Ray players very well\\". I'm a hawk when it comes to watching my finances. It has nothing to do with being frugal, but I have specific goals in mind... some big, like saving for a house in the NYC suburbs, and some small, like saving for a good DSLR to use for my newborn later this spring (along with the costs that come with that endeavor.) As a result of these goals (and the realities of living at this time in history) I have a checking and multiple savings accounts, two 401k accounts, three IRA accounts, a couple of credit cards, 20+ year-old US savings bonds, an existing mortgage, and a few hard assets to track.    I too was forced to choose another personal finance management software when MS-Money ceased updates recently. I initially tried Mint but found the interface a little slow and klunky. I contemplated keeping Money and just manually updating transactions, but that quickly proved too time-consuming. I had initially balked at Quicken due to all of the negative reviews, but bit the bullet and downloaded the electronic version.    So far, Quicken has been a breeze. There is a document that explains how to prep a Money file for export/import (which is mostly common-sense steps, such as removing old accounts and reconciling all transactions.) The import was basically a two-step process for me: the wizard crunched the file and gave me a log of items that it could not import. In my case, the only changes it made were mentioned in the conversion document beforehand: a few truncated account names, unable to import some recurring payments, and removing some special characters from spending categories. Besides about a dozen transactions that were duplicated or mangled, it successfully imported all 7000 transactions that I had logged in Money.    Moving from the Money interface to the Quicken interface has been mostly seamless. The basics are the same: there are tabs for Home, Spending, Bills, Planning, Investing, and Property & Debt. Each screen provides good information and is customizable. For example, my Home tab shows Alerts and Reminders, an All Accounts overview, a rolling Net Worth graph, a Projected Balance graph of several accounts, and an \\"In/Out/What's Left\\" table (similar information as the Income and Expenses graph in Money.) In addition, you can pin an Accounts List pane to the left or right sides of the screen. So far, it looks as if the information on these graphs is mostly correct. I'm sure that as more information becomes native to Quicken (as opposed to converted from Money) they will become more accurate.    The Spending tab is simple: a pie graph of your expenses over a timeframe, total spending over that timeframe, and a table of how it was calculated. The Bills tab is equally simple and accurate. I have already easily set up some recurring transactions.    The Planning tab contains three sections: Spending Planner, Lifetime Planner, and Tax Center. The Spending Planner is the budgeting tool, which can be set up to automatically create a budget (by analyzing your past spending) or manually. I used the automatic option, which came pretty darn close to my actual spending over the past 12 months. The tool can even skip one-time transactions, which is good if you received a one-time salary bonus, or had a large one-time car expense that you don't expect to recur. I have yet to use the Lifetime Planner tool, but it looks to analyze and recommend changes to reach long-term goals (e.g. retirement.)    The Tax Center looks interesting. It tracks your actual income, deductible expenses and capital gains and, after your tweak them and input some variables such as your exemptions and tax rates, will give you rudimentary tax amounts. I only track my net pay, but I imagine that if I tracked gross pay plus taxes, the reports would be more accurate. I would not trust these numbers when it really came down to brass tacks, but by inputting several numbers manually I found that the reports are close enough for simple tax planning throughout the year (such as, \\"how will the sale of this security affect my capital gains taxes\\" or \\"how will an extra mortgage payment increase my deductions?\\")    The Investing tab is similar to the same tab in Money. It offers customizable views of your investment accounts. I don't find much different here.    The Planning & Debt tab shows some Net Worth graphs (the historical calculations are incorrect due to changes made during the import.) The Account Overview and Debt sections give some other graphs and tables. This is the place where you add new loans and new loan payments.    There is no Reports tab, but there are reports under each main tab that pertain to that category (for example, all of the investment-related reports are found under a button under the Investing tab.) So far, I have found all reports to be accurate and most to be useful.     Setting up the online updates was painless and has worked perfectly so far. It hasn't mangled any new transactions and has posted them to the correct accounts.    Ads? I haven't come across a single one.    Maybe I'm the exception, but I have had no issue that I couldn't easily overcome, no issue with the functionality of the app, no show-stopping issue with the Money conversion. People seem to be unhappy about the \\"upgrade\\" from 2009 and 2010, but as a former Money user, I find Quicken to be a suitable replacement. All it takes is the time to learn a new app.

I was a long-time Microsoft Money user, and a reluctant Quicken 2011 Premier user since late 2010 (once Microsoft announced it was no longer updating Money). Based on scathing reviews of 2012 and 2013 versions, I never tried to upgrade to those versions and have no experience with them. The reviews of previous versions are similar to other reviews for 2014 in that most claim very few (positive) changes hence no real reason to upgrade. Alas, soon my online updates in Quicken 2011 will stop working in April 2014 due to Quicken's policy of only supporting the last 3 versions (2014, 2013, 2012). At least they are consistent - this has been their policy for 10+ years. I love automatic updates of my accounts, so I bit the bullet and purchased Quicken 2014 Premier.

I think a lot of people are in my shoes... Waiting as long as you can (3 years) before being forced to upgrade from 2011 to 2014 due to the syncing capability expiring, and begrudgingly upgrading and wondering if it will make your life better or worse. So this review is written from that perspective... 2011 vs 2014.

First of all, the upgrade process was fairly straight-forward. I didn't lose any data, there were no errors, and all customized reports came across just fine.

I don't get too worked up over cosmetic or even functional changes but instead put the effort into learning the new application and generally am OK with whatever changes the vendor makes in the long run. In this case there REALLY isn't anything to worry about - Quicken 2014 looks almost identical to 2011. There are a few minor changes such as color scheme. More accounts show up in the account bar (new \\"Separate\\" group for accounts that don't show up under \\"Banking\\", \\"Investing\\", etc. groups). Some dialog/input boxes look different but offer the same functionality. One annoyance is that the pencil/blue dot in the register to indicate Manually Entered / Reviewed downloaded transaction sometimes gets covered up by a new balloon tooltip that prevents you from getting the context menu that allows you to mark it as Reviewed. But overall, it looks very similar.

The One Step Update process is a bit different - one less dialog to click through (especially if you are using password vault) - so that is good, but it does look different. I can't tell that it is any faster at updating accounts than 2011, however. I have been having problems updating my PayPal account in Q2011, and in Q2014 it still had problems but generated a lot more error dialogs that kept getting in my way, so I ended up disabling syncing of my PayPal account altogether.

There is now a way to close accounts instead of only hiding them. This helps in reducing the number of accounts to choose from in account droplists, for example.

I also like the ability to see upcoming scheduled entries in the register - very nice enhancement, although I haven't worked with this too much yet.

The mobile app... I have an Android phone, and it is nice to see recent transactions and such, but really nothing too exciting here. My wife has an iPad and I have to say the iPad app is actually pretty nice - I was pleasantly surprised - very smooth and fluid and modern. The main way we use it is to keep track of our monthly budget/spending progress. Our original (default) budget had way too much detail & too many categories in it, so we created a new and separate \\"Discretionary\\" budget that had limited categories (dining out, gas, etc but not fixed things like mortgage) to make it easier to view on the iPad. It is nice that you can determine which one (and only one) budget to sync to mobile devices. This is nice since Quicken is on my laptop and I travel quite a bit, so it is easy for my wife to keep up-to-date on everything while I am away.

Many times when syncing, Quicken will hang and/or crash. I can't seem to spot a consistent condition that causes this to happen. Again, I haven't lost any data, but this behavior doesn't instill confidence, either. At one point I was running into enough crashes that I ended up disabling mobile sync (Quicken Cloud syncing) altogether to essentially reset everything, then re-enabled mobile Quicken Cloud syncing. Since then, it has been a bit more stable, but not perfect. The initial sync takes a LONG time... be prepared to wait 10-15 minutes even on a high speed connection (100Mbit up/down office connection), but the incremental sync after that is reasonable (less than 30 seconds). I am syncing 17 accounts and the small \\"discretionary\\" budget.

Overall, I'm not mad that I upgraded, but not ecstatic either. I wish it were more stable and efficient and that there were a real competitor out there to keep Intuit on their toes. Overall it has been an OK experience.

I was very excited when Amazon announced their unlimited cloud service.  I immediately began my trial but was very disappointed when I saw how hard it was to actually access your files. While this is still a great storage solution for large files which you will not frequently access, it lacks the ability to pick and choose which file you would like to download from your cloud to your computer if they are larger than 5GB or consist of more than 2,000 files.  If you would like to retrieve a file that is larger than 5GB, you will have to download your entire cloud to your computer!  This can be a major problem if you are low on hard drive space, as this will essentially mean that the program is holding your files hostage until you have sufficient disk space to accommodate your entire cloud, or delete files from your cloud until you do.  In conclusion, if the shortcomings of this program/cloud service do not bother or apply to you, then Amazon cloud drive will serve you well.
