The initial update led to a converted QDF file where large portions of transactions in many of my accounts were simply blank - the accounts showed rows of blank information. I spent more than 1 hour on the online support (which I have to say was supportive). The result was that my converted file was simply unusable. Thank God for backups!!! I had to recover my backup, uninstall Quicken 2013, and reinstall Quicken 2012. Next after making a copy (File > File Operations > Copy), switching to the copy, validating the copy (File > File Operations > Validate and Repair), then attempting to update to 2013 again.
At this point things seemed better (no blank transactions). However, I then downloaded transactions from one of my financial institutions and more problems began. After verifying and accepting unmatched transactions, I accepted all transactions and a dozen transactions wouldn't \\"process\\". Quicken reported them as \\"broken\\" and advised deleting them. Ok. One transaction simply became undeletable and unchangable. If one changed any of the fields you couldn't exit the transaction. You had to kill the Quicken appliction and restart it. I made another connection to Intuit's Chat support.
Three hours later I had uninstalled Quicken 2013 again, repeated the whole process above following Support's directions and gotto EXACTLY the same place. Interestingly, after validating the QDF file in 2012, updating to Quicken 2013, converting the file(which involves a validation step), then immediately validating the converted/validated file, the validation report indicates multiple \\"Damaged data block\\"s. Support advised me, \\"do not run the validation process unless recommended by Quicken Support.\\" Yes, I laughed!
Ultimately I asked for a refund which they rapidly granted. I uninstalled Quicken 2013 and reinstalled Quicken 2012.
I recommend that you do not purchase Quicken 2013. I might anticipate some problems with release 1, but release 8?!? Completely unacceptable! I am severely disappointed. So much so that I am writing this review, the first ever I have written.

Outlook 2013 has what I consider to be a pleasant design (although I would prefer a much darker theme and more color choices) but lacks the connectivity for which I was hoping. I have two important e-mail accounts that I was hoping to use with this product: a personal Gmail account and a Microsoft Exchange account for my work, and that's where I ran into trouble.

In the case of the Gmail account, I was saddened to learn that Google and Microsoft disagree about the future of e-mail, calendar, and contact protocols and they're largely inoperable out of the box. I was able to configure e-mail by falling back to IMAP/SMTP but there are some known issues where Gmail accounts will slowly get out of sync and changes won't mirror to the server properly. For contacts, I found a free third-party program called GO Contact Sync Mod that was able to synchronize all of my contact information. I haven't found a solution for my Google calendar yet, but I believe there are some paid add-ins that might do the job. Even with add-ins, though, I would stay away until they fix the IMAP problems if you use Gmail.

For the Microsoft Exchange account, I was hoping it would be a breeze. Unfortunately, my workplace is stuck with Exchange 2003 and Outlook 2013 is not compatible. I'll start by saying that if Office 2003 still existed, I would use it. I am no fan of the ribbon, which has lots of things I don't need, and lacks some of the things I need. (Yes, it's somewhat customizable, but not as much as the menus used to be.)

But this is about 2013, which to my mind is largely a deprovement from Office 2010.

There is however one improvement I can think of: One can now comment on comments in Word, which is a lot better than trying to select the same text someone else selected, and adding a comment to that. (My cat is sitting on my lap and trying to type, so if you read here about more improvements, that's her opinion. My mileage may vary.)

Ok, so the deprovements. Do a web search for "ugly office 2013" and see how many hits you get. About 43 million on Google (no, that is not an exaggeration.) The icons look like something you'd find in a VGA-era program, and faded as if they'd been sitting out in the sun that long. The interface is available in three almost indistinguishable shades of battleship gray. You can choose some kind of artwork for the top of the window, which is about as helpful as painting daisies on the aforementioned battleship.

The menus (ok, top-level ribbon labels) are in UPPER CASE (I haven't seen this since the Apple I).

When you want to open a file, or do a save-as, you switch to some other view entirely, where you can't see the file you've been working on.

The top bar on the window no longer changes colors depending on whether the Office app has keyboard focus--I can't tell you how many times I've tried to delete a message from Outlook, or a word from Word, and I've instead deleted something from some other program I have open--because I can't tell by looking whether the Office app has focus. (Ok, if you change your Windows scheme to a high contrast scheme, it will change, but then lots of other things--like web page backgrounds in browsers--are invisible.)

And finally, good luck if you want to change the size of an Office window. Used to be you could grab any border with your mouse and drag it. You still can, but you have to play with the mouse until the mouse cursor changes--I believe it's because the borders used to be (and still are, in non-Office apps) several pixels wide. But the Office borders are a single pixel, making it very hard to mouse them.

So those are the UI problems with this. Granted, Microsoft has to do something every few years to make people want to buy a new version. What could they have done that would have made me want to use it? Several things: fix legal numbering in Word, fix styles in Word, add a better method for moving emails to folders in Outlook, add styles in Powerpoint, and add commenting in Powerpoint. (I'm not a big Excel user, so no opinions there.)

Legal numbering is the kind of section numbering in which the first level sections are numbered 1, 2, 3..., the second level sections 1.1, 1.2..., 2.1... and so forth. It's used in lots of disciplines, not just by lawyers. And in all the decades of Word's existence, this has never worked right. When one bug gets fixed, another is introduced. The current system is simply incomprehensible. I think you have to define each level, but the directions (on websites where this is discussed) are long and complex, and IIUC separate the numbering style from the heading style. I'm increasingly using LaTeX, and there *it just works*. Why Word can't make it just work, I don't know.

Styles are supposed to be a way of maintaining consistency in formatting of complex documents. For some reason, "Normal" is the default style, which is wrong (Body text should be, because that's what you usually type). That's always been a problem, but Word 2013 (or maybe 2010?) introduced several more problems. Titles, subtitles and section headers default to a bewildering range of odd fonts, colors, italics etc. (Why did they think I wanted blue section headings?) Yes, you can change all this, but why shouldn't it come out of the box with some reasonable defaults? If you use the styles palette, it defaults to a recommended set of styles; whoever decided what was recommended must not write the kind of documents I write. I have to change the options to display "all styles", and even then I have to choose to sort them alphabetically instead of by "recommended." (If I don't want to use just the recommended styles, why would I want to see them in the recommended order?) And finally, the styles seem to sometimes work, and sometimes have no effect. If you have the cursor in a paragraph, and click on one of the styles, the paragraph should immediately adopt that style. For reasons I haven't worked out, this doesn't always happen.

Moving emails to folders in Outlook: If you have five or ten folders, it isn't too painful to drag an email to one of those folders, and there's even a list of recently used folders, or you can create a list of "favorite" folders. But I've been at my current company for almost ten years, and I have hundreds of folders, arranged hierarchically. And while I haven't accessed some of those folders in years, I probably go to fifty or more different folders in a week. I swear the icons that toggle whether a folder is open (so you can see the sub-folders under it) get smaller with every version. (It can't be that I'm getting older.) At any rate, it is painful to mouse around looking for the right folder, and scrolling the folder list if I've got a long list of folders open. (Like lists of employees, or non-employee people I know, or other organizations, or...) A fix would be to implement a typing-based search tool, like the Nostalgy plugin for Thunderbird. (Oh, and the search tool will tell you what folder an email is in, but not what the hierarchical path to that folder is. Good luck finding the folder if yours are deeply nested, like mine.)

Styles in Powerpoint: Have you ever watched a PP presentation where the font sizes keep changing from one slide to the next? That's because the only way to change font size (or other font characteristics) in PP is to select some text and set its font size. Why can't Powerpoint have styles, like Word does?

Comments in Powerpoint: We send slide sets around, and while you can sort of embed popups in the slides, it's not as easy to use as it is in Word. 'nuff said.

Bottom line: When I can, I use either LibreOffice (which has its own problems) or LaTeX. Both are free. If you have a choice, I recommend you do the same. But I'm giving Office 2013 two stars, not one, because it is usable if you have to use it, and it has reasonable functionality (if you can find it in the ribbon).

After many calls and lots of digging on the internet, I just discovered why the Norton Anti-SPAM doesn't do anything. My problem has been that while I mark e-mails as SPAM, and they go into the blocked list, but the next SPAM mail comes into my in-box and sits there.

Based on what I see on Google, this is a common problem. It turns out that Norton only can watch the two (antique) e-mail ports that hardly any e-mail service now uses. Those are 110 and 25. When you try ot add the right ports, it claims those are used by other applications (which is nonsense). None of the three services I routinely use support those any more. Norton claims that hey can't watch the SSL/TLS ports now used, because they can't see encrypted content. That's ridiculous for several reasons. Once in my in-box, the e-mails are not encrypted...so much for "Outlook integration". It also means that if I use the secure ports my providers insist on, then I can't use Norton Anti-SPAM...the whole reason I bought Norton 360 in the first place.

So, it's now gone from my systems.

It does teach some basic vocabulary and has the option to record your voice and replay it, but don't expect to be able to communicate after studying with it.
It teaches the words and phrases in a vacuum without inserting the words into sentences. When it teaches phrases, it does not tell the learner which words are which. For example, a learner will only be able to say, "Where is the bank?" rather than "Where is the __?" and plug in a different location. It also neglects to teach the answer to any of the phrases, so while a learner might be able to ask where the bathroom is, they will not be able to understand the answer.
Instant Immersion Khmer also makes no use of the Khmer writing system, so learners do not get to see any of the words written how they will see them in Cambodia. It is valuable for learners to see the writing system associated with the words. Sometimes, even without being able to sound out words, you can learn to recognise them and identify them on a menu.
Khmer is the fifth language I have attempted to learn, and the third with a different writing system, so I have some experience in effective and ineffective ways to learn a language. This program might teach some words, but won't give a learner the basic tool of the most simple communication in Khmer.

First of all, this app is as ssllooooowwww as molasses. Every transaction takes about 5 seconds of "thinking time" before iBank is ready to talk to you again. Second, the interface was designed once, badly, and never revised:

Want to export to CSV or Excel? Sorry, you can't.

Want to create a report from an account's transactions? You'll have to manually (with the mouse!) unclick the checkboxes for ALL THE OTHER ACCOUNTS you've ever had, leaving just the one you want to focus on.

Want to search for a transaction by date, or category, or amount, or payee across accounts? NO SEARCH FOR YOU! You have to create a "smart account" defined by the criteria you want, then delete it when you're done, so that the interface doesn't get even slower. And then you realize you need to see that search result again, so you have to recreate it, and delete it again. "Saved searches", without constant live updating, would be so much better.

And it erases all the checks' check numbers (new behavior in iBank 5, so I suppose this might actually get fixed?). I can't find which "import rule" or "transaction template" is responsible for mangling things, because there are many hundred such rules/templates it created all by itself as I import transactions, and (did I mention this?) there's no way to SEARCH them.

So on the 3rd of May I sat down to check my accounts and Q2012 wouldn't connect to any of the banks I use. I started looking around for a fix because I could understand 1 bank going down but not several. I went to the community forum and searched for an answer and stumbled across the Q2012 nugget that said "we told you so." A little statement that said we told you in the EUA that connections would be lost 3 years after the purchase so you will be forced into buying a product that you may not want. Not at all happy about that and I don't really know if that is an Amazon or Quicken deal. Either way, be up front about it and don't stick that in a 5 page end user agreement that seems to give you the freedom to do whatever. As another reviewer said, Quicken is about the only game in town. I'm sure there are others but it's like Windows was (the most used, most popular piece of stuff out on the market). Downloaded the product and installed it. That part was easy; then it went through its install questions as if you had never been a Q user before. So starting from that point I was not happy but it finally asked if I was an Intuit "member" and allowed me to use my previous ID and password to get started. Next it wanted to know if I wanted to use my old password for my password vault to keep prying eyes off of the accounts... turns out this is just a way to keep the files locked until you want to actually see them before you update them (I'll have to find a way to turn that off). Next it converts your old 2012 files into a new file and you get to start all over with your bank accounts and restarting the web express or direct download. Surprisingly, once you go to TOOLS-> ACCOUNT LIST and get your account to edit, it highlights your bank name so you think you can hit next and reestablish connections. NOPE. You have to retype your bank name and then hit NEXT. And of course it finds your accounts under your username and password but it doesn't initially allow you to link the new files with the old accounts (my checking, my savings, my whatever) so I end up with my old accounts and 3 duplicates with only a 60 day history. I had to go back and start again but this time it allowed me to link the accounts so my accounts are all in place with all of my history from 1995. Next step was to delete the duplicates. At least that went OK. After the first account was set up, I tried the other accounts (after converting each file) and used just the "one step update" tool. That worked a lot better. Pretty seamless, actually. I was able to link accounts to the old named files and all went well. Then everything synched to the cloud (I thought I might use the IPad app since the two are supposed to work together). I installed the app on the IPad and found I could only see one account. That bites! and the app doesn't give you account details, only a summary. Apparently, Intuit wants you use the one step update tool only because it has taken the account actions drop down menu away (on the top right hand side of each account)  and replaced it with a little gear icon. You have to do some exploring here and I think the "named" drop down menu is better than the gear (this is a desktop version, not a smart phone version). Aside from those quirks and irritations, it appears to work basically the same. I downloaded a trial version of this program (from the manufacturer's web site) primarily to see how well it could record screencasts so that I could burn some training videos on CD. Although I was aware it did other things, I wasn't initially focused on those other features because I already owned more expensive (and sophisticated) video editing suites which I planned to use for editing and compiling the resulting files. Using only this product, I was able to record audio/video from multiple sources (screen captures, webcams, cell phones, even professional video cameras!), split, join and perform simple editing on them, compile them and publish them to CD, DVD, cell phones, etc... All these capabilities made purchasing this a no-brainer!

Don't get me wrong - this program can't do any of the more advanced editing, special effects, titling, and other functions that programs like Pinnacle Studio or Sony Imagination Studio series can. But for common tasks that most users will do, this is probably all you need, plus it's MUCH easier to use.

If you don't need every function this program offers, you can get individual elements of this program separately at a lower price (see the manufacturer's web site, \\"HELP Center\\" Tab, \\"How to Chose Your Program\\" topic for how they are broken down) but this bundle price is hard to beat. If there is any chance you might need the others, this is the most cost effective way to go.

Before you buy this, I strongly recommend doing a lot of research. If you are using OS X 10.9.2 or later and don't have TWAIN compliant scanner drivers, you will be dead in the water after initial install. Starting in with OS X 10.8, it looks like Apple decided to switch to ICA (Image Capture) drivers. You MUST install the 11.0.4 update at a bare minim to support ICA devices. The better option is to install the latest update, currently 11.0.7.

If you are scanning over your network (your scanner isn't plugged in directly via USB) and are using OS X 10.9.2 or later, there is a known issue where Adobe Acrobat will crash about 2-3 seconds after the scanned image appears in Adobe Acrabat. The ONLY fix is to plug the scanner into your USB port.

I went from a working solution using Adobe Acrobat X with older HP Twain drivers running OS X 10.9.3 on a 2010 MBP to Adobe Acrobat X with the same printer/network setup on a brand new MBP. It didn't work.... at all. After I got everything working (installing the updates and switching to a USB connection) it seems like it may be faster, but that could be due to the newer hardware.

Bottom line: If you've got an existing setup using Adobe Acrobat X that works with your scanner, there is no real difference that merits the purchase of Acrobat XI.

Are you scanning over a network? Don't buy this
Are you using OS X 10.9.x? Don't buy this
Are you using an HP photosmart all-in-one? Don't buy this.

If you do decide to buy, research your hardware combination ahead of time.

Here is my review, originally posted in March 2014 and now mysteriously missing from the Amazon review pages.

As a loyal Quicken user since 1997, and one who buys the new version every year, I am astonished at how bad this new release is. With each new release, Quicken works well and I can safely ignore negative reviews. NO LONGER! The number of new usability problems introduced with Quicken Premier 2014 (on Windows 7) is so large that it seems clear the product was rushed to market to meet Intuit's annual new release (new revenue?) deadline without performing sufficient quality assurance. Below I will list the problems I have discovered so far, and I will update my review if and when any new interim releases resolve these problems.

KEYBOARD SHORTCUTS ARE BROKEN IN THE REGISTER VIEW. The Register view is the bread and butter of Quicken: this is where you enter and review transactions. Common functions such as cut, copy, and paste of text fields (Control-X, Control-C, and Control-P) do not work - I must use the mouse and select these functions from the Edit menu (which still lists the keyboard shortcuts). Similarly, Control-R does not bring up the Reconcile window, Control-J does not (always) bring up the Bill and Income Reminders window, Control-S does not bring up the Split Transaction window, Up-Arrow and Down-Arrow keys do not shift focus to adjacent transactions, etc. These problems are especially noticeable when switching to another application, then back to Quicken.

KEYBOARD FOCUS IS LOST IN THE REGISTER VIEW. If I highlight a text field such as Payee or Amount, then switch to another application and switch back to Quicken, the highlighted field is no longer active. This means I must use the mouse to re-select the field before I can begin typing a value. It's often the case that I will switch apps - for example, when reviewing a credit card statement and comparing transactions. This particular problem makes me think the name"Quicken" should be changed to "Slowen".

DOWNLOAD TRANSACTIONS / BILL AND INCOME REMINDERS PANE IS ~ALWAYS~ PRESENT. When switching to the Register view from one account to another account, this pane at the bottom of the view is always presented in maximized form, which minimizes the number of transactions I see in the Register. Previously, this pane only appeared when there were unprocessed downloaded transactions or active reminders for the account. It's annoying to have to close the view every time I switch between account registers to review or enter transactions. I can see 10 transactions (2-line display) with the pane closed, but only 3 transactions when the pane is open.

DOWNLOADED TRANSACTION RED FLAG. After One Step Update, Quicken shows a red flag for accounts with new transactions. Sometimes I will see the red flag, go to that account register, and find NO downloaded transactions (particularly for investment accounts). If I perform One Step Update again, or just select Update Transactions, sometimes the new transactions will appear as expected.

ONE STEP UPDATE FAILS CONSISTENTLY FOR SOME ACCOUNTS. I have seen numerous errors for Wells Fargo Bank and PayPal. I have disabled and re-enabled One Step Update for these accounts numerous times, with no improvement.

ATTACH RECEIPT TO TRANSACTION. I became a huge fan of this feature in the previous 2013 release. I could scan a paper receipt or document to a PDF file, attach that file to a transaction, and discard the receipt. After attaching the file, a Quicken window would display the receipt, providing instant confirmation that the correct file was attached. But in Quicken 2014, the attachment shows up only as a generic PDF icon. To verify the attached file, I must double-click the icon to open Adobe Reader. To view any existing attachment, I must click multiple times to bring up the external Adobe Reader. On the support chat rooms, Intuit says the newbehavior is necessary to support attaching other file types such as photo images taken with smart phones. Really? This is the same Quicken product that uses a built-in (and very antiquated) web browser to navigate to the web sites of financial institutions (rather than simply launching your favorite browser). Can't they include a PDF and JPG viewer in the application?

As of March 28, 2014, I'm using the latest R7 version of Quicken Premier 2014 for Windows. As I stated at the top of this review, I'll update this review if and when any of these problems is resolved in an interim release. For the time being, avoid this release and stick with Quicken 2013 or earlier.

I haven't had time, but perhaps someone could compare this to the free ZygoteBody (the old Google Body, currently at zygotebody.com). They seem very similar although Visible Body breaks the anatomy down by system.

It seems to include the major anatomy divided into the 10 major systems. It has a bunch of pre-defined views of the anatomy and allows you to zoom in and out. The viewer interface is similar to Google Earth. One major drawback is that there is no orientation indicator. For example, when I went to a view of the skeletal hand, I initially couldn't tell whether I was looking at the palmar surface of the right or the dorsal surface of the left. Of course, I figured it out based on the anatomy, but you get the idea that there is no overall indicator of your orientation relative to the major anatomical planes of the body. This is especially important since the default left mouse button behavior is to rotate the model rather than pan.

A major limitation of the software, as far as I'm concerned is the lack of information on the connective tissue holding everything together. For example, in the spleen there is no indication of the attachment of the peritoneum, the splenorenal ligament, or the gastrosplenic ligament. The liver does have the major ligaments named, but the attachments are not shown. If you are interested in the attachments between the organs or the mechanical interactions of the organs, this is not the software for you.

Also, in case you weren't aware, this is a static, 3-D \\"picture\\" of the body. Imagine the old \\"[[ASIN:B004ZETWLK The Visible Man Model Kit]]\\" that you might have had as a kid. This software is like having that model (with the plastic organs and all) with a computer to describe to you what it is you're pointing at. You can't move the joints, you can't jiggle the organs, you can't clip off an artery, etc.

Finally, unlike Google Earth, you can't add annotations to the model.

Regarding the software itself, every time I run the software, it pegs one of my quad processors at 100% (effectively using 25% of my available computing power). This is independent of whether it's in the foreground or even whether I'm interacting with it or not. There is no disc or network activity. I can only assume that this is a result of poor programming and effectively slows my whole system down. Not very neighborly when I'm trying to actually get work done on the computer while I review anatomy. In a nutshell, it has unacceptable processor requirements. I really hope that they fix this in the very near future.

I am not sure if it's the server or win10 though. Other than OneNote, there are also lots of bugs such as office or windows activation. Some other apps didn't work at the first place as well, such as the best known windows companion Drawboard PDF. After seeing two of my most heavily used apps struggle under win10, I say enough is enough, I am going back to win8.1.

Let's face it, if you've used Microsoft Office in the past then you know pretty much what you're getting with this software. There is nothing revolutionary or life changing about the 2013 version of this software. There are minor tweaks here and there, but nothing to get excited about. It works as it should.

But, the biggest difference that I noticed was that this new version is non-transferable between computers, and you can only install it on 1 PC. In past versions, you were able to make one software purchase and outfit your whole household (up to 3 PCs) with Microsoft Office. No more.

This 2013 version clearly states that it is only for 1 user, and 1 PC. So, if you have more than one PC in your home, you will need to make multiple purchases of this software. Also, if your computer dies or you decide to replace it with a new one, guess what? Yep, you guessed it, you'll spend another $140 to re-install Office2013 on your new computer.

I am a fan of Microsoft Office programs, and I've used them for many years, but this new \\"non-transferable\\" policy is an important thing to know when making a buying decision. I hope this review has been helpful.

UPDATE 3-19-2013:
Microsoft has recently changed its user agreement allowing you to transfer the software to a different computer. If your PC dies or you get a new one, you can transfer the software license to the new computer. While this is a step in the right direction, unfortunately this is just a half-measure. The policy still only allows installation on just 1 PC, contrary to previous versions which allowed installation on up to 3 PCs. Those who have more than one PC will still have to make multiple purchases.

Amazon has one of the most robust cloud strategies in the world. The trouble is, most of their technology is not geared at consumers. The strange thing is some of their competitors in the consumer market use Amazon as their back-end.

As it stands today, this download is basically confusing and half-baked. It serves only one purpose. You drag files into it, and it uploads them into your account. When I launched the program, it told me I had about 150 MB of space left (yes MB... not GB), but it had links telling me that it's now "Unlimited" for Prime Members, but that wasn't clear either. Apparently unlimited only applies to photos. Videos and other files are not unlimited. They give you 5GB for that. 5GB isn't even enough space for 10 minutes of high definition video, so if you have a photo library that has videos, you're going to need to upgrade to the next level... the true "Unlimited" version, which is $59 per year.

Assuming you get past all that, all this program does is let you upload your files by dragging them. It doesn't sync, so you'll have to remember which files you uploaded, so you can remember which ones need to be uploaded later.

Once the files are there, that's it. It doesn't actually let you do anything with them within the program itself. It gives you links to their web site to view or download them. One interesting thing about the website link was that it not only showed me files uploaded using this program, but it also shows you any personal documents such as PDFs and ebook files that you've uploaded to your Kindle. It's interesting, but not useful, because I can already do that on the Kindle itself.

I think Amazon needs to re-think their consumer cloud strategy. It seems to me that they need to decide if they are serious about building a consumer cloud product. As it stands right now, DropBox, OneDrive, iCloud, Google Drive, iDrive and others are far more consumer friendly, and useful.

I've followed the thread started by M in SC for the past 4+ months.  I've even posted a few comments.  And now I just finished my own taxes.  Tax year 2014 is finally closed.  By now, the controversy about crippling Deluxe and the multiple bungled responses from Intuit have been discussed to death.  I don't have anything to add that hasn't already been said in some of the thousands of comments.  I hope Intuit fixes this for tax year 2015 and the lesson sticks for future years.  This isn't the first time Intuit has tried to pull a fast one on customers and been caught.  There was a TT controversy a few years ago about printing additional tax returns.  And Quicken/Quickbooks - the file format changes with every new version, so once you upgrade you can't go back and you become a slave to whatever mandatory bundled services come with the new version.  And every upgrade seems to have more required services bundled in.  One good one - with Quickbooks, the Intuit self-service payroll service is only good for three years.  If you're a Quickbooks customer and you use Quickbooks for payroll, even self-serve payroll - you must upgrade to the new version every 3 years to keep getting payroll updates.  But this review is for Turbotax Deluxe, not all the other Intuit products.  And for me, overall, it worked.  I called the toll free number early and Intuit gave me a free upgrade to Premier, so I was able to deal with my Schedule E and Schedule K1.  That worked.  The installation went smoothly, the interviews asked all the right questions and, near as I can tell, all the forms looked good.  I e-filed my federal taxes and US Mailed my state taxes.  A text message came to my cell phone a few hours after e-filing that it was received, so the process was smooth.  If I have to install TT on some other computer in the future and do something with my 2014 taxes, that will be a problem - but it's unlikely.  And I have PDFs of all the forms.  Finally, there's Turbotax VP Bob Meighan.  Bobhas been the public point man through all this and he's taken a great deal of abuse.  Kudos to Bob for staying engaged and mixing it up, even in hostile territory.  So overall - the software did its job and was easy to install and use.  Bob Meighan is a visible spokesperson and he gives the best answers he can give, at least with product functionality related issues.  That's worth five stars.  But Intuit created a trust issue and I don't like looking over my shoulder for hidden gotchas.  How am I supposed to trust software from a company I'm worried is trying to screw me? I'm a hobbyist woodworker with a large format CNC Router.  I've been looking for a capable CAD/CAM software package that I can legally use at home. I spent months looking for software that I could reasonably afford that wouldn't cost me as much as my cnc machine to use.  I found it in Fusion 360.  Fusion 360 is a new kind of software platform for Autodesk.  Rather than a pricey up-front cost strategy, they are offering several subscription services ranging from free to (currently) $40/mo or $300/year.  The free license is available to hobbyists and "start ups" which means you can use the software for free as long as you aren't making a profit with it.  If you do end up developing a product for sale, you can roll into the $40/mo or $300/year subscription which is quite affordable even for the adventurous hobbyist like myself.  As far as the software is concerned, It is really quite good especially if you consider the price.  It is not as convenient to use as something like Inventor.  It lacks hot keys and other powerful features like parts libraries.  It also has a bit different kind of assembly methodology using "joints" rather than constraints.  A joint is basically an automated way of doing 3 constraints at once which can be convenient, but can be frustrating as well when you want to do more complex constraints.  That said, it is an EXCEEDINGLY powerful software package.  There is nothing better in the CAD market for under $2-3K for the cad capabilities and absolutely nothing like it for under $4-8K on the CAM side.  It is a fully parametric, fully direct modeling, and fully T-Spline sculpting CAM package with assembly capabilities as well as a model based integrated CAM system.  Further, it is a product that is growing in capability all the time.  It may not be the perfect software for enterprise level work yet, but for the hobbyist and small shop, its more than enough especially at the price level of free.  I do a lot of woodworking and this software is great for making technical and sculpted parts.  However, there are certain things I wish it did that I have been told are coming:  1) V-carving... This is nice for making lettering and signs.  You can do embossing, but making really good letters is not easy at the moment.  2) Part patterning/nesting... when you cut stuff out of sheet stock you really want to make the most of your materials.  Right now, there is not an easy way to even pattern parts with the same CAM operations.  If you need multiple parts, you either have to create a specialized gcode program with work offsets yourself or machine them one at a time.  3) Feeds and speeds calculator... You need this to keep from breaking or burning up your bits.  Right now I use G-Wizzard by CNC Cookbook.  It would save time if Fusion would do an even basic calculation to set these for you.  Because of these short comings, this software is not ideal for CNC routers, but I've been told that these things are coming so maybe I will revise my review to be a full 5 star review when these features are complete because then I would need no other software to do what ever I want.  **** UPDATE **** This morning I got an update of the software.  There is now a CAM Patterning ability.  Maybe it was there before and I didn't notice it, but I just found it this morning.  That is a BIG plus.  I have upgraded my review to 4.5 stars.  I can live without a feeds and speeds calculator as I have one already, but being able to pattern parts in sheet goods is HUGE.  I hope they do a nesting feature too.  If only they did v-carving, I would be super happy.  If they had a sculpting library available for relief carving I would be EXTATIC.  Maybe this is coming too.

If I could give this product ZERO stars, I would do it. Until this summer, when my computer melted down, I had 20 years' worth of data in a Quicken file, and had been struggling mightily with an old Mac and Quicken 2007 (Q2007). Many of you who are longtime Mac users know the problem: Intuit has not really cared about its Mac customers for years. First they left us high and dry when Apple released OS 10.7 and Intuit supplied no upgrade for many, many months, while trying to sell us on the vastly inferior Quicken Essentials (QE). I reacted the only way I could, which was that I didn't upgrade my OS. Better to have an old OS than risk all those years of financial data going down the tubes!

I was very excited to hear about Quicken 2015 (Q2015), but it turns out that Q2015 doesn't provide even the basic functionality that Q2007 did. You'll read elsewhere about reports being insufficient. That's true. They're terrible. But the real problem is that Q2015 has abandoned double-entry bookkeeping and has instead created a needlessly complicated "transfer" process to move money between accounts. WHY IN THE WORLD WOULD YOU TAKE SOMETHING SO ELEGANT AND SIMPLE AND MAKE IT NEEDLESSLY COMPLICATED?!? In Q2007, to transfer funds between accounts you just needed to use the bracketed [Account Name] in the "category" portion of the register and Quicken would create mirror transactions: a debit in one account and a credit in the other. Better yet, if you were transferring money into an investment account, you could buy shares using that very same entry. Now, in order to accomplish the same thing, you'll need one entry to provide "cash in" to your investment account, and then a second one to "buy" shares of your investment. So what used to be simple, with just one entry, now requires two.

The real weakness of this is evident to anyone who has a Q2007 file that gets "updated" in Q2015. This new version of Quicken will not understand your entries. When you "update" your accounts with your investment house, your totals will be wildly off, and you will have to change EVERY SINGLE investment transaction to create TWO transactions on the same date.

This is insanity. Mac users would be satisfied with an updated version of Q2007. Just give us WHAT WE ALREADY HAD SEVEN YEARS AGO, but this time with tech. support. Or at least updates every now and then. I don't even need all the stuff that PC users say is so cool about their version of Quicken... just give me WHAT I ALREADY HAVE, ONLY UPDATED, so banks and investment houses will continue to link to it.

Quicken is asking which features we'd like to have as Q2015 is upgraded gradually. Let me try to answer that: Why would you not START with the product you had in 2007 that was successful? Provide ALL those features. We want something that provides a seamless transition from Q2007, and Q2015 won't do that if you muck around with it this much. Stop trying to reinvent the wheel.

Oh, and if you must upgrade Q2015 gradually, then your FIRST upgrade should be to return to double-entry bookkeeping.

TurboTax contains a current bug in the Wisconsin state version. If you have HSA account income, the program will not transfer the correct income amount from your Fed form 1040 or 1040A to the Wisconsin Sched I form. The income error can be directly overridden on the Wisconsin Sched I form, but when you do and attempt to eFile your state return, TurboTax will accept your $19.95 eFile payment, and then it will block you from eFiling the state return with the overridden (correct) income amount on Line 1 of Sched I.     This has been reported to TurboTax Tech Support and they refuse to acknowledge any issues with the program. All you receive in response is a canned email saying they don't have enough information to determine if this is a bug and you should contact Tech Support again. Contact tech support a second time, and you'll get the same canned response as the first time.     If you buy this, don't count on eFiling a correct Wisconsin return, but if you don't mind paying more tax than you should, then go for it!

Hi there.  Wondering if you should buy this after reading the mixed reviews?  READ ON!  That's why I wrote this...    About me:   I am a quicken user for...well...dude honestly, I don't know how long.  Going back to the very first versions.  Back in the early 90's, and for a few years, I was a guy that was tracking my checking accounts and budgets with custom spreadsheets.  I've used several versions of Quicken (and a couple early versions of MS Money).  I've also used Mint, both online and the mobile app.  So, I know a little bit about personal finance software.    Why I bought this version:  I have been using Quicken 2007 for 4 or 5 years off and on.  About a year ago, after a few months of toying around with Mint, I fired it up again and started really buckling down on my checking accounts.  I'm very tech savvy (15 year IT professional), so naturally after I had started using Quicken again, and realizing my version was so old, I started looking at upgrading.  After reading so many terrible reviews about 2010, I decided to stick with what I had. There were so many things that I wanted 2007 to do, that ultimately curiosity got the better of me and I decided to give 2011 a try after analyzing the positive AND negative reviews.    Let me preface my opinion of this product with a couple of things.    #1) I am not an MS-Money user.  Many of the negative reviews I saw about Quicken were in relationship to disappointed MS-Money users.  To be honest, I really liked Money back in the day and it was my first choice for an upgrade.  When I found out Microsoft had canned MS Money, I decided not to upgrade at all (but eventually went with 2011).  In any case, my review takes into account no comparison with MS Money.  If you are not a MS Money user like me, then you can disregard many of the ill reviews by those users like I did.    #2) I am a 2007 user.  MUCH has been improved on this version, and it has been working VERY well for me.  It's not a downgrade or inferior versionat all.    #3) I do not download transactions from the bank.  I tile my bank website and Quicken windows and just balance my transactions manually.  Now, I'm not what you would call a very organized person and I do this once every 3 days or so.  It works for me and if you're a more organized and have more attention to detail than I do (which you probably do) then you will have no problems using this software to balance your accounts and budgets.  There are some negative reviews out there as they pertain to matching records from downloaded bank transactions.  I have no opinion on the matter other than I prefer to do it manually.  If you work with Quicken like I do, then you can disregard quite a few more negative reviews.    #4) I don't trade/invest/etc., so I don't use Quicken for that. If you are like me, then you can also disregard a couple of negative reviews.    #5) I don't sync Quicken with anything.  If you don't do that either, then disregard a bad review or two as well.    #6) I don't work for Quicken.  I'm a very disorganized, Computer Technologist with \\"swipe-a-holic\\" wife.  I DESPERATELY need a way to reconcile my checking accounts, balance my budgets, and project the status of my income on any given day.    About the product itself - it's very good and you can see what acquiring the Mint software has done for Quicken if you are familiar with it.  Most notably, there is a planning tab that lets you set up a comprehensive budget that you can use to keep track of your spending just like Mint.  It's useful if you can figure out how to use it.  For the not so computer-comfortable, it may prove to be a challenge trying to understand what it's doing.    This version also allows you to set up budgets and savings goals.  I sat down for about an hour with these trying to figure out how to use them.  Ultimately, they seem too complicated and cumbersome for practical use.  And between the planning tab and my accounts, Quicken 2011 does everything that I need.    Things that I like about Quicken 2011  - It's much less hokey than 2007 and much faster.  The screen doesn't flicker hardly at all and it opens much faster.  - The calendar view is much easier to read.  The boxes are bigger.    Things that I REALLY like about Quicken 2011  - I can move bills around that have flexible due dates without affecting all occurrences of it.  - I can search for individual transactions and edit them in the register.  I'm not sure if 2007 could do this, but for the life of me couldn't figure out how (and I'm a tech guy)  - The integration of Mint's budget/planning feature.  It works VERY well if you know how to use it.  - I ***L-O-V-E*** the \\"Bills\\" tab. The graphical stacks of bills that you can cycle through, how they have \\"Paid\\" stamped on them, and how it lists all your bills on an easy to read and very customizable view are all VERY nice features.    Responding to certain negative reviews:  - The program IS NOT slow at all.  Not compared to 2007 or any other software that I use for that matter.  - I don't see any spyware, advertisements, or hidden government propaganda.  There is a Free Credit report icon that it put on my desktop...but for the love of CHEESE...get real, don't look in my window/privacy paranoid people.  You don't have to click on the link and a large, reputable company (WITH EVERYTHING TO LOSE) like Quicken is not going to steal your monies.  - It has not crashed on me, does not lock up my computer, and does not cause my other programs to stop working.  YOU people who are complaining about that sort of thing need to stay off the \\"FREE MOVIEZ DOWNLOADZ\\" sites and whatnot, or wipe your computer and reload Windows because your problems are beyond Quicken.  By way of example, I installed it on my Wife's computer that the kids are always on...it has all sorts of things installed, is very clumsy, and I have no problems with it.  - I had been using Quicken 2007 for years.  I forgot to do a backup before I installed 2011.  I installed the new version carelessly clicking away and *tada* it was accurate up to the last time I reconciled my account.  In other words - it imported my old information quickly, flawlessly, and with no extra effort on my part.  I have no idea how or why other people complain they couldn't do this.    - What is this missing Cashflow tab?  I've been using 2007 and I don't remember this thing.  In any case, it is just as functional (and even moreso) than my 2007 version (which was great).  I can't see how I could get or use any more information out of the interface options that it has.    - The software does what it's supposed to do and it looks fine.  It doesn't have big animated buttons, glossy vibrant color schemes, or a bouncing paper-clip to guide you through it.  But Quicken has never been like that.  I'm sure that it purposefully looks like professional software you might find on banking computers because...well, it is sorta supposed to be financial software now isn't it?    My complaints or gripes if you will:  -I haven't figured out how to (or if you can) set up one-month budgets on the planning tab.  Budgets seem to continually roll over when I create them.  -I don't like how the prior month's bills that just happen to clear the next month come up on that month's budget.  -The savings/budget thingie seems useless.  It creates a whole other account, but you have to transfer money into it from other accounts?  And confuse the heck out of your register?  I dunno...I gave up on that thing. lol  But whatever...it's not a game breaker for me.  Not with all the other features.  -I wish when you searched for multiple transactions that it would allow you to FULLY edit them right there in the results view.  You can search them one at a time in the register and change anything, but you can only change the \\"Payee\\" field on searches with multiple items.    All that and there's much more to be pulled out of this software.  I may fool around with it some more in the coming months/years, but this version works fine.  From my point of view, I'd say the overall rating on this product needs another star because not all of the complaints apply to everyone.    Hope that helps anyone out there like me that was looking to upgrade an older version (2007/2008-ish). :0)

Good things
--You can download a good PDF manual, which I did before I bought the product. It gave little warning of some of the things I would encounter.
-- Slo-mo works very nicely
--You can browse and view footage that is stored on your computer.
--When you find one you want to use, you can drag and drop to the program.
--You can preview and split a clip while it's in the \\"library\\" and not yet in the timeline.
--Screen capture bundled with the program allows for capture at 15, 25 or 30fps. Also allows for full screen or selected area. Is easy to set up and works well. You can save to program library and also to a folder of your choice.
--The program does a lot of things. So do a lot of other programs. So that really isn't too much to get excited about.
--There are some cool features like object tracking, which is very nice for NFL announcers to analyze plays, but somehow I don't think I'll ever find a use for. Especially since it is a very blunt instrument which easily strays from the intended object to be tracked (a surfer on a wave--high contrast, should be easy; fails to follow very well).

Things that made me give a low rating:
--The manual available is for the Pro version, not the Ultimate version, which supposedly has more features. So how do I use those features? Who knows?
--Resuming Play after Pause (or Pause after Play) in preview window creates a short blackout of the preview window. Irritating, distracting, and I hope it's not a sign of bad things to come.
--Settings>Preferences>UI Layout...
Not allowed to change anything. All options are grayed out except for Default which is permanently selected (Radio Button). So much for user preference.
--The preview window is very small, too small to see details. And you can't make it larger. In comparison, Adobe Premiere Elements 12 allows you to resize the window (drag the edge) as large as you want. Very useful, one might say essential, for editing details.
--Can't change viewing speed of video in preview window. This is an extremely basic concept and essential for editing--slow it down so you can stop where you want to stop without having the reflexes of a quick-draw target shooter. Searched the manual and online and found nothing, so it seems that it can't be done. For comparison, Adobe Premiere Elements allows this--all you do is use the L or R arrows on your computer keyboard to nudge or run backward or forward.

--No way to reduce the video and audio sample clips to a simple list. Either they're hidden, or they take up the space.
--Video and image samples are stacked on top of any visuals I put in the \\"library\\" so that to do any work I first have to scroll down past all of them each time. They are so useless and such a hindrance that I ended up deleting all of them. Corel even made this hard by not allowing me to select more than one at a time, and delete one at a time.
--Trimming function is awkward and counter-intuitive.

If you are in Edit mode and make the mistake of clicking on Options>Attribute, you will find your screen loaded with bright, blinking samples--exactly the kind of visual distraction you don't want when you're trying to get some work done. This wouldn't be so bad, but you can't make them stop. You can click on Options (to close it), Video (to switch to another editing function); you can right and left click all you want on FX--nada. When you come back, the obnoxious blinking samples are gone. But your work flow has been disrupted. Again.
--When you split a clip and save each portion, the first portion ends with a number of frames of severe jaggies. So you end up with less useable footage than you shot. This is a disaster if you are shooting long continuous scenes that need to be divided and saved. And sometimes in real life that's what you need to do. This problem doesn't occur with \\"primitive\\" free programs like Virtual Dub.

If you insert it into the video, it's of obviously inferior resolution. I can do better by running a video in MS Viewer, and using MWSnap to do a screen shot, which can be saved as TIFF or JPEG. I'm a semi-truck driver, and needed a good mapping program. Compared to this program - Delorme Street Atlas USA (2014), Microsoft Streets and Trips is the better of the two.

I tested each by mapping a standard trip that I frequently make: from Sumner, WA to Great Falls, MT. My truck is governed at 62 mph, and I customarily drive this route in 10 hours and 50 minutes - a single day trip (DOT rules don't allow me to drive more than 11 hours). The trip is 651 miles.

Delorme maps this trip at 696.38 miles. It does not take the logical routes of WA-18 or MT-200, no matter which route setting I select ("Shortest" or "Quickest").

To follow the Delorme route would cost me 45 minutes, and I could not have finished the trip in one day. Also, considering that diesel is now nearly $4 per gallon, the Delorme route would have wasted 7 extra gallons of fuel (45 miles / 6.5 mpg) - at a cost of approximately $28. The Delorme product can be manually tweaked by "Via" points, but I shouldn't have to do this.

I returned the Delorme product (thanks, Amazon!), and bought Microsoft Streets and Trips instead. I personally find it more intuitive and easier to figure out than the Delorme product. I mapped the same trip (Sumner, WA --> Great Falls, MT) and it mapped it perfectly, using both WA-18 and MT-200.

Another advantage of the Microsoft product is the after-market work on the Points of Interest. If you Google "The Points of Interest Mega File," you'll see what I mean. They have added a LOT of trucker-friendly (and RV-friendly) information, such as Walmarts that allow parking, Costco, Sam's Club, Cracker Barrel restaurants, Rest stops in each state, etc - things that might not have been included in the original released version. Literally thousands of new entries. Nice!

The one complaint that I have about the Microsoft product - and the reason for the 4 stars instead of 5 - isthat the POIs don't include Churches in the "find nearby places" list. This was a surprise to me - especially considering some of the other rather obscure categories that were included. (The Delorme product did list Churches, but did not distinguish between denominations - it was a mess, but it was there.) The Microsoft product didn't list any Churches at all.

I switched to H&R Deluxe this year after seeing that many were severely disappointed with TurboTax. You will probably see this trend almost globally as you research and decide what tax prep software to get. I'll admit, I could have shopped around a bit more, and I may have been able to get away with a lesser product than H&R deluxe, but I don't regret my purchase.

I have only been doing my taxes for 5 years, and generally only have jobs and school forms to file with. Simple W2's and sometimes the 1089T. I always file 1040A. This year was no different - I filed my (one) W2, itemized some deductions for work, travel, donations, and others, and worked through the software. I did have some issues with adding a vehicle in one block, but not being asked about it for a second form where it was supposed to show up again as a deduction. This kept recurring, and I had to manually open the official tax form documents within H&R Deluxe (Which is a handy feature if you really need to get nitty-gritty). I was able to fix it, but I did have to remove and re-add vehicles twice. This is one of the major benefits of e-filing though, as your returns are checked over with a fine tooth comb (electronically) and checked for any definite errors, and then give you some warnings about some potential errors.

I'd say overall, the software was slightly less 'friendly' than the web-based TurboTax I had used for the last few years, but it seemed more in depth - just required more searching on my own. I'd much rather deal with these minor inconveniences than support the business model that TurboTax decided to go with this year. Clearly, I did not have any complicated tax situations or large business transactions to file in this year.

It is worth mentioning that I also prepared my fiance's taxes in a matter of about 20 minutes after I had become familiar with the software on my own return. She had a single W2, and 2 1098T's, with a few charitable donations.

A few other notes to mention that you may be wondering:

-Yes, I was able to import my T13 (return from 2013) file directly into the software, which was created by TurboTax for last year's return.
-Yes, it does include 5 federal e-files with the download or disc version. On the download version, it sent me an activation code right after downloading the product, in a new browser window. I used this to activate the software and get me my free federal e-files.
-It does NOT include any state e-files. It includes one free state download to PREPARE your state, and from there you can send the return snail-mail for free. I chose to efile, as is recommended by Michigan for insuring that there are no errors and for speeding the process up. This cost me 19.95 to my credit card in H&R, or 19.95+a 39.95 processing fee if you're broke enough to need to have it withheld from your federal return.
-The total ADDITIONAL cost aside from the software, for efiling both state and federal for both my Fiance and I: ~40.00
-BACK UP THIS YEAR'S T14 FILE WHEN YOU'RE DONE!!! There is an export button in the program and I strongly recommend doing that, as well as printing your official return, or saving the PDF files. I chose to save mine locally as well as uploaded them to my favorite cloud service. I believe there is a way to link your return into your 'My Block' account, but I could not figure it out after creating the account, so I will just import the file next year. I prefer to be in control of my important documents anyways.

I hope this helps! Unfortunately I can't tell you much as to the business side of this - I'd assume you accountant types can read the fine print and figure out the best version anyways.

One of my New Year's resolutions this year was to start getting serious about my budget.  Most of the people in my family seem to manage their money well, but I have never stuck to a long-term budget or really definitively outlined my financial goals.  I decided to make a budget.  Then, I realized that tracking financial transactions would be key to making wise spending/saving/investment decisions.  I decided to buy Quicken ($60 is what they charge for the Deluxe Edition on their website - they do not sell the Starter Edition.)  I got directed to Amazon and, funny, just happened to have a $25 gift card that I got as a door gift at our holiday party - so, this cost me $.57 out of my own pocket.  I think that might give you some perspective as you read this.    Positives:  This program is significantly less expensive than most.  It does not make you overpay for features you might not need.  If you do not own a home, do not have investments, have sophisticated needs, etc., then you should be pretty happy based on the value.  This program syncs with your bank account and gives you a record of all of your transactions.  This hasn't been problem free, but it is a pretty solid system overall.  It pretty accurately codes your debit card transactions by category - things like housing, food (and alcohol), auto, insurance, health, entertainment, etc.  You can also go back and review certain categories and sub-categories, which makes catching any categorization errors an easy task.  You can apparently have several accounts - I've only entered one so far, and I believe that you can input your charge cards as well, although I have yet to do that.  This is a good tool for tracking spending and seeing where your money goes.  It also allows you to set-up budget by category and compare it to your spending.  I need to explore it more. As a long time Photoshop user, I was looking for a competent replacement as I am no longer involved in a job role that mandates having access to the latest Adobe CC offering. Adobe CC is great---but I certainly don't need to spend $120 a year just for Photoshop and Lightroom ($10 a month for Adobe's lowest package offering), and there are competent replacements for the other Adobe products that don't require a subscription.

Having used some of Serif's products in the past and had a good experience, I took a chance on PhotoPlus X6, thinking that it should be able to duplicate most of what I was looking for.

For the projects I work on I am most interested in non-destructive filter and layer effects. In terms of the "raw" features I need, PhotoPlus X6 hits most of the major checkboxes---non-destructive effects for bevel, dropshadow, saturation, contrast, color balance; a reasonable assortment of brushes; ability to do fast and easy pattern stamping. The interface is mostly in the same vein as Photoshop, which is a plus, since it's what I'm used to, so I felt at home almost immediately using it.

As long as you approach your use of the program from a reasonably "casual" viewpoint, the app shines. Quick adjustments, a crop here or there, a minor content replacement there, and everything works and runs reasonably smoothly.

However, as soon as you start to push the envelope at all, things don't go so well. First, I wouldn't recommend attempting to do anything with images larger than 10 megapixels, simply due to the speed of the rendering engine. Simply put, images that I used to edit in Photoshop with dozens of layers and adjustments at 12 megapixel sizes simply chokes on PhotoPlus. Changing layer states, moving between tools, ANYTHING you do when working on large sized images with layers and effects takes 3-5 seconds just for the tools to respond.

Like I say, for simple, minimal adjustments the speed difference is negligible, but once you start adding on layers and effects, Photoshop quickly pulls ahead as the superior choice for speed.

For me the speed difference is by far the most troubling, but there's other niggles that get under my skin. One, there's no text on a path support, which I use extensively; you're basically limited to straight-line text. Two, the blur tool simply doesn't work in any way that feels intuitive compared to Photoshop. Photoshop's blur tool feels intuitive and "right" out of the box; I had to spend a good hour fiddling with the various tool settings to get PhotoPlus's to come anywhere close to it (and it still doesn't work right).

While Serif's non-destructive pattern/bump mapping layer effects can create some impressive visuals, doing something as simple a texture pattern overlay layer is an exercise in frustration.

All told, PhotoPlus X6 ends up being exactly what you'd expect from a company running from behind the market leader---for the price it's a decent piece of software, but it's nothing to rave about. The "big picture" features and tools are there and mostly work as intended, but moderate to power users will find themselves wistfully sighing for the elegance and usability that's missing.

Level Set: As many others here, I've been a long-time Quicken user. I'm reasonably techically savvy having worked as a software developer for 30+ years and have been a PC owner since 1982. In years gone by, Quicken was an outstanding application. When lots of applications at that time were fraught with operational and especially, human factor, problems, Quicken was a marvel of reliability and operational ease -- way ahead of the curve. Things have changed since then.

Again, as many others, I updated from Quicken 2010 only because of the pending cessation of online banking support. I purchased Premier 2013 and downloaded it from Amazon. As an aside, I've always been pleased with the service from Amazon, and the problems I note here are unrelated to Amazon.

Installation has been one problem after another. Unfortunately I didn't keep completely detailed notes of the activity, so my description of the activity will be a bit hit and miss.

The download consists of a small installer which then actually loads the main Quicken executable. This download process completed without problems, although it did take quite a bit longer than I would have expected via my relatively capable broadband connection.

Upon completion of the download, the installation began. The installation consists of three steps which are monitored on the display:
Uninstall of the existing Quicken,
Install of 2013, and
Install of 2013 updates.

Install of 2013 updates never completed -- just hung near the end. No way to easily recover. Couldn't cancel. Had to reboot via task manager.

After restart, clicked on Quicken Premier 2013 desktop icon (which had gotten installed) and got message saying downloaded executable could not be found, and I needed to redownload from the Amazon library which I did. Eventually reloaded and same problem occurred with the \\"Install 0f 2013 Updates\\" portion not completing. Sometime during this process I saw an error messages saying \\"Quicken failed to install FIDIR.TXT, a required online banking setup file. Please reinstall Quicken. If problem persists, contact Quicken support.\\"
I tired to do this , but discovered that Quicken support is available only Mon-Fri 5 am to 5 pm.

Searched around the web and saw a reference to FIDIR.TXT sometimes not being activated because of a permission problem. The reference further indicated that the file resides in Program Data/Intuit/Quicken/Common/...(I forget the rest of the folder name). I looked there and indeed discovered that I did not have permission to see the file. Messed around with advanced permissions for a bit and eventually was able to modify the permission appropriately.

I tried the reinstall again, and it eventually worked. (there very likely were other intervening problems which I since forgotten).

I restarted the application and, at least superficially, it appeared to be operational. While looking around, I saw an indication on the display that I should update to R10. I looked in \\"About Quicken\\" and discovered I was at R2. So I clicked on the update to load/install R10 and the system sat there for the longest time giving no indication that anything was happening. After about 10 minutes I had enough and either just cancelled or rebooted (don't remember which).

Restarted Quicken and again saw the indication about updating to R10. Tried again. Same thing -- system just sat there with no indication that anything was happening. After another long period of waiting, I was about to abort the operation when -- out of the blue --the system responded that the operation was complete! Rechecked \\"About Quicken\\" and -- wonder of wonders -- I was finally at R10.

Spent a few minutes more looking at the application and it seems to be operating correctly. We'll see what happens over the next few days/weeks. If anything significant transpires, I'll update this review.

Net: Far too many installation problems. In the old days, Intuit produced an outstanding product. At this point, they're fortunate there is not a reasonable alternative.

Update 3/4/13: R11 doesn't install.
Since getting all the initial install problems sorted out, the application has been running satisfactorily -- up until now. When I started it last night it indicated the R11 was now available and suggested that I install it. I tried multiple times to do this with various problems. Most times the d/l and install appeared to complete properly (although with a completely non-informative progress bar), but \\"About Quicken\\" still shows that I'm running R10 and I continue to get the \\"Update to R11\\" notification. Very disappointing and frustrating.

The help function was a mixed bag for me. This program will not enable you to hold any meaningful conversation with people in Dutch as you will gain no knowledge in grammar or sentence structuring of any sort through this program.

Testing AV software is a hobby of mine. Kaspersky has been consistently among the most appreciated AV products for the past 4-5 years; this edition, though, has some issues with Windows 8 and 8.1 that do not allow the customer to experience its protection fully, or without some tweaks. If you are using an HP Pavilion notebook, Mozilla Firefox, and Windows 8 or 8.1, the chances are that 1) the Kaspersky protected browser will not fully work due to incompatibilities with the HP hardware (and hence you won't be able to do online banking with a full protection), and 2) Mozilla Firefox currently has a conflict with the Kaspersky security certificates and is likely to block every secure connection (\\"https\\") that you open, including sites like Amazon, Google, etc. The solution is to tweak Mozilla to accept Kaspersky's certificate, and even that solution still will leave banking sites inaccessible, unless you open them through another browser.    In terms of detection rates, the program is solid; in terms of zero-day protection, unfortunately it isn't as good. It has a strong firewall that offers an 80% protection according to the rigorous Matousec leak tests (in comparison, Bitdefender gets 19%, Norton 9%, Webroot 23%, etc.). Independent AV labs certify Kaspersky very highly; on-hand malware tests done by a variety of enthusiasts (look at YouTube) do not seem to agree completely.    The product is light and works well; it is a pity that it shows incompatibilities with a number of hardware and software components.

Searching: iMac

However, once I reinstalled my MICROSOFT operating system, I had no issues installing MICROSOFT's office suite. Switching to a three-month free trial of University was no issue once that one-month trial of Home Premium was up.

ISSUE #2 They recommend a minimum RAM for this, I think 1GB. My laptop has 8GB of RAM, and it still slowed down considerably when Microsoft Word was running and I was trying to edit pictures in a document. Clearly this product was designed for almost only the high-end laptops, and even barely for those.

ISSUE #3 Instead of installing the product and downloading the occasional service pack like with previous versions, this version has you download the software from the Internet (which takes a couple hours on a 1gbps Ethernet connection) and then downloads updates as they arrive. This creates major issues for the program. For the past several days it's told me to \\"click here to install updates\\" (a bubble at the bottom of the screen where the clock is). So I click it and it disappears without doing anything. Finally, yesterday it decided to install the updates. Normally when a program updates one needs to restart their computer. However, it never told me, so I didn't. I tried using Office, and it told me that it had \\"stopped working\\". So I tried to do the built-in \\"repair\\", which froze on \\"quick repair\\". I Ctrl+Shift+Esc to close the program and had to restart my computer. When I went in to try and repair it again, it told me to wait until it was finished, when I had already closed it and it couldn't have possibly been doing anything. So, taking what I'd learned from many failed installs, I downloaded Microsoft's \\"Fix-it\\" to uninstall Office from my computer. I then went online to deactivate that install and re-installed it, without issue.

SUMMARY: Microsoft clearly has a lot to fix with this. The original installation issue apparently is rather common, and can be extremely aggravating, especially if you're a college student trying to download it and needing to get to work. The picture editing isn't too annoying most of the time and can be worked around a little(by the way, Microsoft has improved their built-in picture editing quite a bit--one of the main good things about this new suite, as well as the templates). However, the updates virtually corrupting the whole Office Suite??? Considering how long and frustrating it was to fix, this is something that makes the entire product rather unreliable, especially for a college student. After my trial, I might go ahead with the purchase since it's so cheap, but I continue to have Open Office installed on my laptop as backup because I never know when Office 365 will decide to stop working on me.

If you already have another, older office suite, stick with that one. Don't buy this one until the major bugs are all fixed, unless you decide that you can deal with the issues.

If you are receiving this error, don't bother contacting Sehkhomang from tech support. That's the person I got. I know, that's what I was thinking. I told him/her to forget about it, and I decided to figure it out myself. Well, if you open task manager, and view the network activity while updating your bank account in Quicken, you will notice that there will be no network activity as long as you do not have any other programs connected to the internet. This means that the problem is on your end, not the bank. I stated by shutting down my virus and firewall program. Update was unsuccessful. Then I checked windows firewall to make sure it was off; it was. I then logged into my router. I am very careful about my security so I have hardware securities set in my router as well as software on my computers. I then started un-checking securities one at a time, updating the router, and checking to see if I could update. It was not successful till I enabling all tunneling options. I recommend that if you don't know how to enter your router, or if you don't understand the security features, you should contact a IT professional. If you have them read this review, they should understand what is keeping you from connecting to your bank. Enabling tunneling is not necessarily a security risk. Tunneling is used as a security feature. There may be another cause for this problem, but this did fix my problem, and Quicken support did not even mention security being a possibility.

Next year I'm definitely going to fill out my returns with both H&R Block and TurboTax's online web app for free before I pay anyone to file my returns.
